She does not lie and she does not bully; she arrives at the table having already worked out the two worst outcomes available to you, sets them both down in front of you with enormous warmth, and waits. Animals come away from Willow's table having agreed to the less bad one and feeling, on the walk home, that they chose it. Half the harbour was bought that way. Pebble's family, who have had the crossing for seven generations, have a standing rule about never meeting her without a third animal present, and will not say which year they made it.
characters.voice: Big, warm, expensive. Uses your name twice a sentence. Lays out your options in ascending order of how much she would like you to take the last one.
characters.arc: Five rungs, from one ferry to the whole harbour. The Ferry Trader at 1 and the Tide Reckoner at 3 are Otter tempo — a paw free, a shift moved. From the Toll Keeper at 2 the table starts working on the animal across it: a card of theirs goes back on top of their deck, because whatever they were holding is not the thing they are going to be talking about now. The Harbourmaster at 4 puts both bad outcomes on the table and one of them happens, and the Harbour Admiral at 5 does that every morning and takes a cut of everything the Capital City sells.

wantedArt.why: The Admiral is the office rather than the quay — the leases, the licences, an otter behind a desk too large for the room. It carries neighbors/12, Willow on the quay, as a stand-in.

wantedVerbs.verb: opponentChoice (a rival picks which hardship they take)
wantedVerbs.why: The maker asked for a card that makes the other Mayor choose between losing Supply or another hardship. Two things are missing: nothing on a Character can take Supply off a rival at all — `everyoneLosesSupply` is a Disruption's shared shock and `giveSupplyToOpponent` runs the other way — and no effect offers a rival a choice of branches. Every reaching verb in the vocabulary (`makeBusy`, `opponentTopdeckFromHand`, `unemployOpponentCharacter`) simply happens to them.
wantedVerbs.workaround: The choice became a toss. The Harbourmaster and the Harbour Admiral put both bad outcomes on the table with `coinFlip` — an animal goes back to work, or a card goes back on top of the deck — so the pair is real even though the rival does not get to pick which. Roger's ha'penny is the borough's own method for a call that will not come down on its own, which makes the seam a thing the town already does rather than a thing the engine could not do.
wantedVerbs.resolved: Built, both halves: `opponentLosesSupply` takes Supply off a rival and tells them it happened (`onSupplyLost` fires for them), and `opponentChoice` puts two branches on the table and lets the rival pick which one they take. The Harbourmaster offers 2 Supply or a card back on top; the Harbour Admiral offers 3 Supply or an animal put back to work. `power.js` pays the card the least of its branches, because the rival picks — which is also the design rule: print two you would be happy with. Roger's ha'penny stays the borough's method for a call nobody will make; this is the harbour office's, which is to make somebody else make it.

cards.name: Peanut
cards.title: Ledger Apprentice
cards.text: When Peanut completes a shift, put 1 Supply by on Peanut.
cards.flavor: Two paws for the ledger, and a tin behind the desk that nobody is allowed to ask about.

cards.name: Peanut
cards.title: Barista
cards.text: Upgrades Peanut. Whenever one of your Characters finishes a shift, put 1 Supply by on Peanut.
cards.flavor: Everyone coming off a shift walks past the counter, and nobody walks past the counter for free.

cards.name: Peanut
cards.title: Accountant
cards.text: Upgrades Peanut. Busy: take every Supply your Characters have put by.
cards.flavor: Peanut calls it 'bringing the tins in', and has never once been wrong about which tin.

cards.name: Peanut
cards.title: Café Manager
cards.text: Upgrades Peanut. When you recruit a Character, put 1 Supply by on Peanut, draw 1 card, and your next Food or Commerce recruit costs 1 less.
cards.flavor: Nobody is hired in this town without someone at the café saying they were worth it, and the second one always comes cheaper.

cards.name: Peanut
cards.title: Town Comptroller
cards.text: Upgrades Peanut. Whenever one of your Characters finishes a shift, gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Peanut audited the whole borough, found everyone underpaid by a little, and fixed it in an afternoon.

cards.name: Peanut's Standing Round
cards.text: Requires Peanut and a Commerce Character. Gain 2 Supply, then you may pay 2 Supply to raise one of your open bids by 2.
cards.flavor: Peanut buys the round, the room talks, and by the third cup everyone knows what the lot is really worth.

cards.name: Oatmeal
cards.title: Ward Clerk
cards.text: When Oatmeal is recruited, your town braces: the next shared shock passes it over.
cards.flavor: Nine of them at the table and never once a head uncounted.

cards.name: Oatmeal
cards.title: Safety Inspector
cards.text: Upgrades Oatmeal. Busy: your Characters cannot be sent to Unemployment by an effect until your next turn.
cards.flavor: He walks the ward every morning of his life and writes down what he finds, every morning of his life.

cards.name: Oatmeal
cards.title: Jazz Singer
cards.text: Upgrades Oatmeal. When Oatmeal becomes upright, the next 2 Supply an opponent's effect would take from you is not taken.
cards.flavor: Four of his brothers and sisters behind him, a Fox on the piano, and a room that forgets what week it has had.

cards.name: Oatmeal
cards.title: Town Warden
cards.text: Upgrades Oatmeal. At the start of your turn, your town braces: the next shared shock passes it over.
cards.flavor: The river came up twice this spring. Both times the ward was sandbagged before the bell went.

cards.name: Oatmeal
cards.title: Borough Alderman
cards.text: Upgrades Oatmeal. At the start of your turn, your town braces for the next shared shock, and your Characters cannot be sent to Unemployment by an effect until your next turn.
cards.flavor: Oatmeal took the chain of office, thanked eight people by name, and asked whether the crossing outside the school had been repainted.

cards.name: Barnaby
cards.title: Night Auditor
cards.text: Hired from the Capital City; enters Busy. At the start of your turn, look at the top four cards of your deck and send any of them to your Town Dump.
cards.flavor: Ask about the ledgers and learn nothing. Ask about the serials and lose an hour.

cards.name: Barrow
cards.title: Stonecutter
cards.text: Hired from the Capital City; enters Busy. While Barrow is upright, your first bid each turn counts as 1 higher. At the start of your turn, Buildings cost you 1 less.
cards.flavor: He priced the whole lot from the pavement, in his head, and was under by nothing at all.

cards.name: Bean
cards.title: Espresso Puller
cards.text: Busy: one of your other Characters turns one step toward upright.
cards.flavor: Bean has not sat down since the postcard arrived.

cards.name: Bean
cards.title: Barista
cards.text: When Bean becomes upright, one of your other Characters turns one step toward upright.
cards.flavor: Three orders behind, certain it is all coming apart, and somehow everybody is served.

cards.name: Bean
cards.title: Café Proprietor
cards.text: At the start of your turn, one of your other Characters turns one step toward upright.
cards.flavor: Their parents' name is still over the door. Bean has never once considered taking it down.

cards.name: Bean’s Coffee Break
cards.text: Requires Bean. Two of your other Characters each turn one step toward upright.
cards.flavor: Whatever it is, Bean has decided you are having a cup first.

cards.name: Brett
cards.title: Retained Counsel
cards.text: Hired from the Capital City; enters Busy, and goes home after three of your turns. Your challenge bids win ties. When an opponent challenges one of your purchases, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Three days of his time is what the borough can afford, and three days is what it takes.

cards.name: Berry
cards.title: Retired Tinker
cards.text: When Berry is recruited, Berry cannot be targeted by an opponent's effect until your next turn.
cards.flavor: The retirement lasted a fortnight. The clock from the guild is already in pieces on the bench, improved.

cards.name: Berry
cards.title: Clockmaker
cards.text: Upgrades Berry. When Berry becomes upright, look at the top three cards of your deck and put them back in any order.
cards.flavor: Berry does not guess what is coming next. Berry simply knows what order things go in.

cards.name: Berry
cards.title: Committee Volunteer
cards.text: Upgrades Berry. When Berry is recruited, you may rehire a Character from your Unemployment for 2 less Supply.
cards.flavor: They went to the meeting to object to being put on the committee and came home as its secretary.

cards.name: Berry
cards.title: Consulting Engineer
cards.text: Upgrades Berry. Busy: the next shift you complete produces 1 extra Supply.
cards.flavor: Berry listened to the boiler for a while, tightened one thing, and would not say which.

cards.name: Berry
cards.title: Workshop Elder
cards.text: Upgrades Berry. While Berry is in town, your Characters cannot be sent to Unemployment by an effect.
cards.flavor: Nobody is let go from a bench Berry is standing at. It has been tried.

cards.name: Berry
cards.title: Guild Warden
cards.text: Upgrades Berry. When Berry becomes upright, you may rehire a Character from your Unemployment for 3 less Supply, and one of your other Characters cannot be targeted by an opponent until your next turn.
cards.flavor: Berry stands in front of the youngest one on the bench and asks, mildly, what exactly the guild thinks it is doing.

cards.name: Biff
cards.title: Beat Constable
cards.text: When Biff becomes upright, one of your opponent's Characters is put back to work, turning one step away from upright.
cards.flavor: Biff comes down the lane and everybody finds something respectable to be doing.

cards.name: Biff
cards.title: Chief Constable
cards.text: Upgrades Biff. When Biff becomes upright, two of your opponent's Characters are each put back to work, and you may rehire a Character from your Unemployment.
cards.flavor: He stopped the trouble, walked them home, and by Friday had found them something to do.

cards.name: Biff
cards.title: Cadet Constable
cards.text: A short shift: 1 turn, 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Two paces behind Biff, saying nothing, learning the only part of the job that can be taught: the names. He was on the beat for a year before he was allowed to speak on it.

cards.name: Bob
cards.title: Gate Attendant
cards.text: Hired from the Capital City; enters Busy. While Bob is displayed in the Capital City, every pledge in an auction must be one step more expensive than usual. While Bob is upright in your town, your opponent cannot raise a pending bid.
cards.flavor: He is not refusing you. He is asleep against the bar, which from where you are standing comes to exactly the same thing. Hire him and the bar is still down; it is simply down on the other road.

cards.name: Brooke
cards.title: Dock Hand
cards.text: When Brooke is recruited, another Character you control is upright at the start of your next turn.
cards.flavor: Bottom of the rope gang, top of the list of animals who will still be here at six. The licence is only two years off, she says, and has said for eight.

cards.name: Brooke
cards.title: Ferry Hand
cards.text: Upgrades Brooke. When Brooke completes a shift, draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Four crossings an hour and a different great-grandmother's cup story on every one. She learned the whole river's history standing up, in ten-minute pieces.

cards.name: Brooke
cards.title: Regatta Caller
cards.text: Upgrades Brooke. Busy: move a shift from one of your Characters to another.
cards.flavor: They needed somebody to call the starts, so she learned to call the starts. She has the whole bank rowing, rowing, and then swapping crews at the buoy, and none of it stops moving for a second.

cards.name: Brooke
cards.title: Balloonist
cards.text: Upgrades Brooke. When Brooke becomes upright, look at the top two cards of the Market Deck and draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: One balloon came over the estuary in her second year on the ropes and she was at the field before it had finished deflating. Three months later she could fly it. From up there the whole river is a piece of string somebody dropped.

cards.name: Brooke
cards.title: Riverwright
cards.text: Upgrades Brooke. Whenever an opponent challenges one of your purchases, gain 2 Supply and draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Somebody told her once that she would never understand a hull until she had built one. It took four years, it put her licence back by four years, and it is still the best boat on the river.

cards.name: Brooke
cards.title: Mooring Hand
cards.text: A short shift: 1 turn, 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: The bottom of the ladder to River Otter, and she has never pretended otherwise: rope, bollard, fend her off, catch the next one. Eight years off the licence starts here.

cards.name: Betty
cards.title: Barn Sweeper
cards.text: When Betty completes a shift, gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: The grange pays by the barn and Betty sweeps three of them before lunch. None of it is for the barn; all of it is for whatever is waiting in the shed.

cards.name: Betty
cards.title: Whittler
cards.text: Upgrades Betty. When Betty is recruited, Betty cannot be targeted by an opponent's effect until your next turn.
cards.flavor: One of the hobbies that stuck. Half the toys in the nursery came off that knife, and so did most of the fuse plugs, which the nursery has not been told.

cards.name: Betty
cards.title: Stump Blaster
cards.text: Upgrades Betty. When Betty becomes upright, gain 2 Supply, then discard a card.
cards.flavor: A season with a mattock, or a hole, a charge and an afternoon. She worked out which she preferred at about eleven and the grange has sent for her ever since.

cards.name: Betty
cards.title: Firework Maker
cards.text: Upgrades Betty. While Betty is in town, your Characters cannot be sent to Unemployment by an opponent.
cards.flavor: The stump money paid for the powder and the powder paid for Blossom Week's finale. Nobody in this borough is willing to be the one who sacks the animal holding the fuse.

cards.name: Betty
cards.title: Powder Chemist
cards.text: Upgrades Betty. When Betty becomes upright, if you control another Science Character, draw 2 cards.
cards.flavor: She finally sat down and worked out why it went bang, which took a winter and improved the bangs enormously. The kite, she admits, had been mostly hope.

cards.name: Betty
cards.title: Land Clearer
cards.text: Upgrades Betty. When Betty becomes upright, gain 1 Supply, and another Character you control cannot be targeted by an opponent's effect until your next turn.
cards.flavor: Four seasons on the far hedgerow and a great deal of noise, and it is the best ground in the borough. She sold it in the spring and is already three exploits past it.

cards.name: Clover
cards.title: Seedling Helper
cards.text: When Clover is recruited, you may recruit a Character costing 1 or less from your hand for free; it enters Busy.
cards.flavor: Four generations on the same strip and Clover on the end of the row with a watering can too big for them, and somebody smaller still holding the other handle.

cards.name: Clover
cards.title: Market Gardener
cards.text: Upgrades Clover. When Clover completes a shift, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: The Saturday stall is not about the stall. It is about the seed money for the two identical beds Clover is going to plant differently on purpose.

cards.name: Clover
cards.title: Community Gardener
cards.text: Upgrades Clover. When Clover is recruited, you may recruit a Character costing 1 or less from your hand for free; it enters Busy. If one does, gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Clover turned the meadow behind the ward rooms into forty strips and handed thirty-nine of them away. Half the borough's gardeners started as the friend Clover brought along.

cards.name: Clover
cards.title: Rocket Botanist
cards.text: Upgrades Clover. When Clover is recruited, you may recruit a Character costing 2 or less from your hand for free; it enters Busy.
cards.flavor: Potatoes will grow anywhere, they say, if you ask them nicely. There is a photograph of this in the Lending Library, and somebody else is in the doorway of it.

cards.name: Clover
cards.title: Master Botanist
cards.text: Upgrades Clover. When Clover is recruited, you may recruit a Character costing 2 or less from your hand for free; it enters Busy. If one does, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Every garden in three boroughs owes something to a cutting Clover once gave away, and every one of them was handed over with the same question: who else is coming?

cards.name: Clover
cards.title: Plot Sharer
cards.text: Upgrades Clover. When Clover is recruited, if you control another Agriculture Character, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Half the borough's gardeners started as somebody Clover brought along to look at something. The strip has been four generations in one family and Clover is the one who keeps giving bits of it away.

cards.name: Clover’s Potato Experiment
cards.text: Requires Clover and an Agriculture Character. Gain 3 Supply, then you may recruit a Character costing 1 or less from your hand for free; it enters Busy.
cards.flavor: Two identical beds, planted differently on purpose, exactly the way Clover's grandmother said was fussing. Hypothesis: potatoes. Conclusion: a great many more potatoes than expected, and somebody new holding the other end of the sack.

cards.name: Clover's Seed Drive
cards.text: Requires Clover. Gain 2 Supply, and another Agriculture Character you control is upright at the start of your next turn.
cards.flavor: Clover hands out packets on the strip all morning and will not take anything for them. Every one comes back as a basket in the autumn, and most of them come back with the gardener attached.

cards.name: Comet
cards.title: Rocket Mechanic
cards.text: When Comet completes a shift, the next Building you buy costs 1 less.
cards.flavor: She took the Crafts hall's engine course twice because she did not think she had understood it the first time. She had. She has never met a machine she did not want to sit inside.

cards.name: Comet
cards.title: Test Pilot
cards.text: Upgrades Comet. When Comet becomes upright, look at the top two cards of the Market Deck. Busy, once per game: Comet readies herself.
cards.flavor: The board turned her down twice. Both times she went away, learned the part they had marked her down on until she knew it better than they did, and came back. The test was: does it go up.

cards.name: Comet
cards.title: Astronaut
cards.text: Upgrades Comet. When Comet becomes upright, look at the top three cards of the Market Deck and gain 1 Supply. Busy, once per game: Comet readies herself.
cards.flavor: She got the seat on the third application and fell over on the way to the launch. She went anyway. From up here the Capital City is a very small market with very small bidding, and she has already read its order book.

cards.name: Comet
cards.title: Bolt Sorter
cards.text: A short shift: 1 turn, 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Before the third application, before the second, before the first: a kitten on the hangar floor putting bolts in the right tin. She knew what every one of them was for by the end of the summer.

cards.name: One Small Step
cards.text: Requires Comet and a Science Character. Gain 5 Supply and draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: One small step for a Cat, taken on the third application by an animal who had already fallen over twice that morning. One enormous mess in the Crafts hall.

cards.name: Comet’s Countdown
cards.text: Requires Comet. Limited 3: at the start of your turn, gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Three. Two. One. (Comet is still doing up her boots. She knows the sequence better than the board does; it is the boots that have never once gone to plan.)

cards.name: Copper
cards.title: Penny Counter
cards.text: Busy, once per game: Copper readies himself.
cards.flavor: Counts the till twice and sleeps in it once. The second count is never about the till; it is about something he meant to put away and did not.

cards.name: Copper
cards.title: Scale Polisher
cards.text: Upgrades Copper. When Copper is recruited, the next Character you recruit costs 1 less.
cards.flavor: An honest measure makes a lasting friendship, and a lasting friendship makes a better price. Copper has never seen any tension between those two things.

cards.name: Copper
cards.title: Weights Inspector
cards.text: Upgrades Copper. Whenever Supply is taken from you, gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: The merchants who used to lean on his scales learned to stop. Whatever comes for your Supply next, Copper had already worked out what it would cost and put that much aside.

cards.name: Copper
cards.title: Arcade Merchant
cards.text: Upgrades Copper. The first purchase you announce each turn may be announced for 1 less.
cards.flavor: He names a figure so mildly that the arcade takes a moment to notice it was a figure, and by then he has moved on to the weather.

cards.name: Copper
cards.title: Market Steward
cards.text: Upgrades Copper. At the start of your turn, the next Character you recruit costs 1 less. Whenever Supply is taken from you, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: The year the bridge went, they came and asked him to open the shelf. He said not yet. He said there will be worse. He lent them the salt on the quiet and the shelf is still shut.

cards.name: Copper
cards.title: Cellar Keeper
cards.text: Upgrades Copper. A steady shift: 2 turns, 5 Supply.
cards.flavor: Salt, lamp oil, candle stock and a shelf of small coin, counted over twice a year and never once opened. This is the card where the cellar simply pays: no trick, no timing, just a Cat who put it by.

cards.name: Dylan
cards.title: River Otter
cards.text: Hired from the Capital City; enters Busy, and goes back to the river after three of your turns. When Dylan is recruited, another Character you control is upright at the start of your next turn. Busy: move a shift from one of your Characters to another.
cards.flavor: He has held the licence since he was absurdly young and will not tell you how. He will tell you a story about how, and it is a very good story, and it is different every time.

cards.name: Rosabeth
cards.title: Herb Gatherer
cards.text: When Rosabeth completes a shift, rehiring a Character from your Unemployment costs 1 less until your next turn.
cards.flavor: A basket twice her size, mint and thyme and something she will not name, and a song the whole row seems to know the end of.

cards.name: Rosabeth
cards.title: Tincture Maker
cards.text: Upgrades Rosabeth. When Rosabeth is recruited, you may rehire a Character from your Unemployment for 1 less Supply.
cards.flavor: The Science hall has been through her notes twice and come away with a list of ingredients and no method. She is entirely relaxed about this. The method, she says, is the singing.

cards.name: Rosabeth
cards.title: Apothecary
cards.text: Upgrades Rosabeth. Busy: return an Event from your Town Dump to your hand.
cards.flavor: She closes the shop by putting every jar back where the jar wants to be, which takes a while, and she has never once thrown a recipe away.

cards.name: Rosabeth
cards.title: Herbalist Physician
cards.text: Upgrades Rosabeth. When Rosabeth becomes upright, you may rehire an Agriculture Character from your Unemployment for free, then draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Half the Hiring Hall's second chances started at her gate with a mug of something and an afternoon on the beds. She charges for the tincture and never for the rest of it, and she sends them back to the ground they came off.

cards.name: Rosabeth
cards.title: Garden Hand
cards.text: Upgrades Rosabeth. A short shift: 1 turn, 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Not a job so much as a place to be put. The beds want doing, Rosabeth is singing at the far end of them, and by the third week you are somebody who gets up in the morning.

cards.name: Bella
cards.title: Forager
cards.text: When Bella is recruited, your next Event needs one fewer Character. If you control no Buildings, gain 2 Supply as well.
cards.flavor: She was seven, the basket was bigger than she was, and she carried it home full in the week the grange had told everybody there was nothing out there.

cards.name: Bella
cards.title: Field Scientist
cards.text: Upgrades Bella. When Bella completes a shift, draw 1 card, and gain 1 Supply as well if you control one Building or none.
cards.flavor: Three notebooks and the recorder, because by the time she has found the right notebook the bird has gone and she is talking to herself about it anyway.

cards.name: Bella
cards.title: Field Recorder
cards.text: Upgrades Bella. Busy: return an Event from your Town Dump to the bottom of your deck.
cards.flavor: Fifteen years of the same square of hedgerow, every visit dated, and she will tell you without looking it up which year the frost came early.

cards.name: Bella
cards.title: Wildlife Warden
cards.text: Upgrades Bella. Busy: return an Event from your Town Dump to your hand.
cards.flavor: The warden's badge changed nothing about her day. She still sits down in the dirt; she just has the authority to tell somebody else to.

cards.name: Bella
cards.title: Ecologist
cards.text: Upgrades Bella. Your first Event each turn needs one fewer Character, and while you control three Buildings or fewer the first Event you play each turn also gives you 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: The Science hall cites her now, which she finds funny, because the finding they cite is that the wood was doing all of this perfectly well before any of us turned up with a shovel.

cards.name: Bella
cards.title: Science Hall Fellow
cards.text: Upgrades Bella. When Bella becomes upright, you may rehire a Science Character from your Unemployment for 1 Supply less.
cards.flavor: Her recordings have been filed and cited by the Science hall for years, so when the hall lets somebody go, Bella is the one who says the name out loud in the right room. She has still never bid on anything in her life.

cards.name: Finn
cards.title: Auctioneer's Boy
cards.text: Busy: you may raise one of your open bids by 1.
cards.flavor: Nine years old, not allowed to bid, and already the only animal in the room who knew what everything in it was worth.

cards.name: Finn
cards.title: Peddler
cards.text: Upgrades Finn. When you announce a purchase, add 1 Supply to it and look at the top card of the Market Deck.
cards.flavor: The clocks were the high point. Six of them, same household, four years, and they still buy their flour off him.

cards.name: Finn
cards.title: Fair Warden
cards.text: Upgrades Finn. Busy: add 2 Supply to an auction you are winning. When a bid is tied, add 1 Supply to yours.
cards.flavor: He keeps the fair honest, which mostly means keeping an eye out for the Finn of five years ago. He knows exactly where that animal would be standing, and exactly what he would do about a tie.

cards.name: Finn
cards.title: Trade Broker
cards.text: Upgrades Finn. Whenever you gain a non-Statue Capital City card, gain 1 Supply. When you announce a purchase, look at the top card of the Market Deck.
cards.flavor: His percentage is small and he takes it off everything, and he knows what is coming up before the animal selling it does. The committee that reappointed him last spring knows precisely that, and reappointed him anyway.

cards.name: Hazel
cards.title: Barrow Hand
cards.text: When Hazel completes a shift, draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: One barrow, no stall, and a route round the bins that took all night and turned up something worth having every single time.

cards.name: Hazel
cards.title: Night Market Vendor
cards.text: Upgrades Hazel. Recruit: draw 1 card, then discard 1 card.
cards.flavor: Everything half price after dark, on the stated grounds that you cannot quite see it and the unstated grounds that Hazel already knows which one you will take.

cards.name: Hazel
cards.title: Market Vendor
cards.text: Upgrades Hazel. Busy: look at the top two cards of your deck and put any of them on the bottom.
cards.flavor: The bottles have no labels and the keys fit no door anyone can name, and Hazel will tell you what the month means before they tell you the price.

cards.name: Hazel
cards.title: Guildmaster
cards.text: Upgrades Hazel. Busy: take a Market card from the City Dump and gain it.
cards.flavor: They ran the guild hall for two terms and never once changed out of the coat they close the stall in. The committee took the minutes; Hazel took whatever the Capital City had thrown out.

cards.name: Hazel
cards.title: Merchant
cards.text: Upgrades Hazel. Whenever you gain a non-Statue Market card, draw 1 card. Busy: look at the top two cards of your deck and send any of them to your Town Dump.
cards.flavor: Half the borough calls the sky-reading patter. The other half has noticed that Hazel is packing up a stall of exactly the right stock three nights before anyone announces the sale.

cards.name: Hazel
cards.title: Market Committee Chair
cards.text: Upgrades Hazel. At the start of your turn, if you control another Raccoon, draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: They have run the guild hall twice and sit on the market committee, and turn up to both in the coat they closed the stall in. The night trade has a voice at daylight meetings because Hazel brings one of its own along and sits it down.

cards.name: Hazel's Night Market
cards.text: Requires Hazel. Draw 2 cards, then look at the top two cards of your deck and put any of them on the bottom.
cards.flavor: The lamps go on, the trestles come out, and for six hours the town can buy anything at all. Hazel shakes on it before the other stallholders have finished counting.

cards.name: Hoot
cards.title: Night Porter
cards.text: Hired from the Capital City; enters Busy. Busy: one of your other Characters turns one step toward upright.
cards.flavor: The knock comes at four. You did ask. Hoot has the list, your name is on it in a very neat hand, and Hoot has never once been late with one.

cards.name: Inkwell
cards.title: Bookmark Keeper
cards.text: When Inkwell is recruited, your Characters advance an extra step at your next Ready.
cards.flavor: Four books open at once and a ribbon in each, and Inkwell can tell you what page every one of them is waiting on.

cards.name: Inkwell
cards.title: Storyteller
cards.text: Upgrades Inkwell. Busy: another Character you control is upright at the start of your next turn.
cards.flavor: The town under the lake, the doors in the hedge, the cousins of the moon. Nine listeners on the library floor, and every one of them up at dawn to go and look for one.

cards.name: Inkwell
cards.title: Night Librarian
cards.text: Upgrades Inkwell. When Inkwell becomes upright, nobody's Characters advance at the next Ready.
cards.flavor: The reading room goes quiet, the hall clock takes its time, and every animal who meant to leave an hour ago is still in their chair. Inkwell has not looked up.

cards.name: Inkwell
cards.title: Astronomer
cards.text: Upgrades Inkwell. When Inkwell completes a shift, look at the top two cards of the Market Deck and at your rival's hand. Busy, once per game: Inkwell readies themselves.
cards.flavor: The Observatory steps, a flask, and a cat who is supposed to be asleep standing up as if the hour were a suggestion. They will tell you they were looking at Ursa; the other Mayor has stopped leaving their hand on the table.

cards.name: Inkwell
cards.title: Keeper of Stories
cards.text: Upgrades Inkwell. The first Event you play each turn that requires Lore lets you draw 1 card, and your Characters advance an extra step at your next Ready.
cards.flavor: Ask whether any of it is true and you will be told, kindly and at length, that it is all research, and that the geography has never once contradicted itself, which is more than the borough's own history manages.

cards.name: Inkwell's Late Shift
cards.text: Requires Inkwell. Draw 3 cards, then discard 1 card.
cards.flavor: The candle burns down, the last of the little ones is carried home asleep, and Inkwell goes back to the chapter they were actually reading.

cards.name: Inkwell's Star Chart
cards.text: Requires Inkwell. Look at the top three cards of your deck and put any of them on the bottom, then draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Charted entirely from the good chair, which means half the sky is missing and the half that is there is right to the minute.

cards.name: Juniper
cards.title: Messenger
cards.text: When you announce a purchase, look at the top 2 cards of the Market Deck.
cards.flavor: Every route in the borough in every weather there is, and not one delivery missed — though there is a note in the ledger about a cloudy Tuesday and a great deal of complaining.

cards.name: Juniper
cards.title: Courier Captain
cards.text: Upgrades Juniper. While Juniper is upright, your first bid each turn counts as 1 higher.
cards.flavor: They still run the fastest route in town. They simply have eleven other animals running it now, and an ephemeris on the wall of the sorting room.

cards.name: Juniper
cards.title: Ward Councillor
cards.text: Upgrades Juniper. Busy: add 2 Supply to an auction you are winning.
cards.flavor: Four committees, two of them chaired, and not one animal on any of them could tell you the moment Juniper stopped being the one who brought the papers in.

cards.name: Juniper
cards.title: Diplomat
cards.text: Upgrades Juniper. Your opponent cannot raise a pending bid.
cards.flavor: They put it to each animal in the room in the way that animal needed to hear it, and by the time they had been round the table twice there was nothing left for anybody to raise.

cards.name: Juniper
cards.title: Stargazer
cards.text: Upgrades Juniper. At the start of your turn, look at the top two cards of the Market Deck; if you control another Science Character, gain 1 Supply as well.
cards.flavor: The Science hall finds it maddening and the Observatory finds it charming, and both have had to write down how often the call comes off. The post goes where it is addressed; the sky says when to set out.

cards.name: Kevin
cards.title: Hired Hand
cards.text: Hired from the Capital City; enters Busy, and goes back to the city after three of your turns. Each shift Kevin works pays 1 less than the last, down to 1. When Kevin is recruited, gain 1 Supply. Busy: add 2 Supply to an auction you are winning.
cards.flavor: He said yes before you finished the sentence and he was at the yard before you were. Three. Then two. Then one, and a fox asleep on the sacks, and nobody in the borough has ever once been cross with him about it.

cards.name: Lynnette
cards.title: Night Printer
cards.text: When Lynnette is recruited, your next recruit costs 1 less Supply, or 2 less if it upgrades a Character you already have.
cards.flavor: Tomorrow's apprentice notices, printed tonight, free, whether or not anybody asked her for them.

cards.name: Lynnette
cards.title: Bookbinder
cards.text: Upgrades Lynnette. When Lynnette completes a shift, your next recruit costs 1 less Supply, or 2 less if it upgrades a Character you already have.
cards.flavor: She got the press cheap because it was broken and learned to mend it because nobody else would, and a mended spine has been her idea of a good evening ever since.

cards.name: Lynnette
cards.title: Lending Librarian
cards.text: Upgrades Lynnette. When Lynnette is recruited, you may recruit a Character costing 1 or less from your hand for free; it enters Busy.
cards.flavor: Thursday, on the floor, about nine rabbits and whoever else wandered in, all the voices done properly. One of them always comes back on the Friday asking how you get a job.

cards.name: Lynnette
cards.title: Master Printer
cards.text: Upgrades Lynnette. Your Master Characters are ready a turn sooner. Busy: draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: The press runs all night and by morning the whole borough is reading the same page, which is why the animal who turns up on Tuesday to do the job already knows how the job is done.

cards.name: Lynnette
cards.title: Press Feeder
cards.text: Upgrades Lynnette. A steady shift: 2 turns, 3 Supply.
cards.flavor: Sheet on, pull, sheet off, four hundred times, and the ballots are done by morning. Lynnette has fed her own press for fifteen years because nobody else does it without a crease.

cards.name: The All-Night Café
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, if you control a Food Character, one of your Characters turns one step toward upright and you gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Bean's, by the Hiring Hall, open when everything else is shut. Peanut keeps its books and works the day counter; Bean owns it and has never once been seen sitting down.

cards.name: The Festival Green
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, gain 1 Supply and draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: It was here before this Mayor and it will be here after, and on any given evening there is a band on it that nobody booked. Entertainment became a study because of what kept happening here after the shift ended.

cards.name: Hiring Hall
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, you may rehire a Character from your Unemployment for 2 less Supply.
cards.flavor: Half its second chances were somebody else's first. An animal who has stopped getting up is sent to Rosabeth's gate, spends a season on the beds, and comes back through this door; and Biff has walked more animals up these steps than anyone has counted.

cards.name: Winter Stores
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: Whenever Supply is taken from you, take every Supply your Characters have put by.
cards.flavor: Copper drew up the list the borough works from — salt, lamp oil, candle stock — and then built the one thing his own cellar has never had: a door somebody else is allowed to open. He says the town's stores are for the town. His are for later.

cards.name: Fresh Batch
cards.text: Requires a Food Character. Gain 3 Supply.
cards.flavor: Out of the oven at five, on the counter at six, gone by half past. Bean does not advertise it and has never needed to.

cards.name: Open Mic Night
cards.text: Requires an Entertainment Character. Draw 2 cards.
cards.flavor: Whatever room will have it, whoever turns up, four of Oatmeal's brothers and sisters at the back. The borough's evenings are not a rarity and never have been.

cards.name: Hedge Apothecary
cards.text: Requires a Hedgehog and a Mouse. Gain 2 Supply and draw 1 card, then you may rehire an Agriculture Character from your Unemployment for 1 less Supply.
cards.flavor: Betty gathers it, loudly, with a charge if the ground is difficult. Rosabeth grinds it and sings over it. Neither will say which half is the part that works.

cards.name: Slack Water
cards.text: Requires an Otter and a Squirrel. Move a shift from one of your Characters to another, then gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Between tides there is a lull just long enough to hand the job to somebody else, and an otter who will take it off you before you have finished offering.

cards.name: Fair Hearing
cards.text: Requires two Civics Characters. Rehire a Character from your Unemployment for free and draw 2 cards. Your opponent gains 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Biff gives his account, which takes a while because he starts with everyone's names. Brett reads the clause. The animal in the dock walks out with a job, which is how it usually goes.

cards.name: Community Oven
cards.text: Gain 3 Supply, then ready one of your Food Characters.
cards.flavor: The borough's ovens are banked overnight and shared out by morning, which is the arrangement that made Food a study and not a sideline.

cards.name: The Bandstand
cards.text: Gain 2 Supply and draw 1 card, then ready one of your Entertainment Characters.
cards.flavor: Lanterns, a rail, and room for a band of five if two of them stand on the step. It was built for speeches and has never once been used for one.

cards.name: Emergency Reserve
cards.text: Put 3 Supply by on one of your Characters. Goes Out of Play.
cards.flavor: Salt, lamp oil, candle stock, and whatever coin is going spare this quarter. Copper will tell anyone who asks that it is nowhere near enough yet, and has been saying so for twenty years.

cards.name: The Tax Assessors
cards.text: On reveal: both Mayors lose 4 Supply. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: They come out from the Capital City with clipboards and nobody remembers inviting them. Copper has met them four times and has never once been surprised.

cards.name: Open Hiring Fair
cards.text: On reveal: each Mayor may rehire one Character from their Unemployment for free; it enters upright. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: Trestle tables on the green and a queue that moves surprisingly fast, because half of it has already spent a season on Rosabeth's beds and is fit to be somewhere else.

cards.name: The Allotment Strip
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, if you control an Agriculture Character, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Four generations of Clover's family have held this strip, and Clover is the first of them to write down what it does in a wet year.

cards.name: Copper's Cellar
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: Whenever Supply is taken from you, gain 4 Supply.
cards.flavor: Under the weights office, stocked since he was an apprentice: salt, lamp oil, candle stock and a shelf of small coin. It was not opened the year the bridge went and it was not opened the winter the Grain Exchange shut — both times the salt went out on the quiet instead.

cards.name: Berry's Bench
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, one of your Characters turns one step toward upright.
cards.flavor: Berry retired, and was back on the bench inside a fortnight. Whatever the borough breaks, it ends up here, and so does whoever broke it.

cards.name: Rosabeth's Gate
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, your next rehire this turn costs 2 less.
cards.flavor: An animal who has lost a place and stopped getting up ends up at her gate, usually sent by somebody, and is put to work on the beds until they are fit to be somewhere else.

cards.name: The Open Mic Room
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, if you control an Entertainment Character, draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Whatever room will have them, a night a week, five in the band if two of them stand on the step. Oatmeal has never once cancelled.

cards.name: The Boat Shed
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: Whenever one of your Characters finishes a shift, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Down past the ferry steps, where the lightermen keep what the harbour office would rather not know about. Brooke has had a key for eight years.

cards.name: The Gate Hut
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, the next card revealed in the Capital City does not affect you.
cards.flavor: A bar, a lamp, and a hedgehog asleep behind both. The gate is shut from six and Bob does not care who you say you are.

cards.name: Rabbit Token
cards.title: Token
cards.text: A Rabbit token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Handed out at the warren door and counted back at the end of the evening, which is the only way anybody has ever established how many rabbits were actually there.

cards.name: Mouse Token
cards.title: Token
cards.text: A Mouse token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Rosabeth keeps hers in the tin the seed labels came in. Bella has never lost one and can tell you, unprompted, the week she was given each.

cards.name: Hedgehog Token
cards.title: Token
cards.text: A Hedgehog token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Bob has four and has never once produced them at the gate, on the grounds that a hedgehog who needs a token to prove he is a hedgehog has bigger problems.

cards.name: Badger Token
cards.title: Token
cards.text: A Badger token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Struck thicker than the rest, because the first batch came back from a Badger winter bent, and Barrow said quietly that this was a thing about the tokens rather than a thing about the winter.

cards.name: Otter Token
cards.title: Token
cards.text: An Otter token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Drilled through the middle so it can go on the line with the keys, which is Brooke’s doing: everything an otter owns has to survive being dropped in the water.

cards.name: Squirrel Token
cards.title: Token
cards.text: A Squirrel token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Peanut has a great many and will not spend one, on the grounds that a rainy day is coming. Peanut is right about this roughly once every four years.

cards.name: Cat Token
cards.title: Token
cards.text: A Cat token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Issued to every Cat in the borough. Inkwell’s has not been seen since the night it was issued and Inkwell is entirely unbothered about it.

cards.name: Owl Token
cards.title: Token
cards.text: An Owl token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Collected at dusk rather than at the Hiring Hall’s hours, after Hoot pointed out mildly that every Owl in the borough was asleep at eleven in the morning.

cards.name: Fox Token
cards.title: Token
cards.text: A Fox token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Finn can tell you what one is worth this week. Kevin has spent his, twice, and turned up cheerfully to ask whether there were any more.

cards.name: Raccoon Token
cards.title: Token
cards.text: A Raccoon token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Hazel has a bag of them, and not one of the bag came from the Hiring Hall. Every single one was found, and every single one is genuine.

cards.name: Agriculture Token
cards.title: Token
cards.text: An Agriculture token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Cut from the same board as the seed labels, and the first batch went out with Clover’s potato beds stamped on the back by mistake. Nobody has asked for the mistake to be corrected.

cards.name: Civics Token
cards.title: Token
cards.text: A Civics token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Biff signs for his and for whoever he has walked up the Hiring Hall steps that week, which is why the Civics ledger never balances and has never once been queried.

cards.name: Commerce Token
cards.title: Token
cards.text: A Commerce token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Copper weighed one, wrote the weight down, and weighs a fresh one every quarter to see whether the Capital City has started shaving them. It has not. He will keep checking.

cards.name: Crafts Token
cards.title: Token
cards.text: A Crafts token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Barrow’s has his thumbprint pressed into the soft side of it, put there the day the borough struck them, because a thing worth making is worth knowing who made it.

cards.name: Lore Token
cards.title: Token
cards.text: A Lore token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Kept in the Lending Library’s long drawer with the ribbons. Lynnette prints the replacements, and the replacements are better than the originals, which Inkwell finds very funny.

cards.name: Science Token
cards.title: Token
cards.text: A Science token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Comet read the specification twice before collecting hers, in case she had misunderstood it the first time. She had not. She wanted to be sure.

cards.name: Food Token
cards.title: Token
cards.text: A Food token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Bean keeps the cafe’s in the till, under the tray, and Peanut counts them with the takings every night whether or not anybody has asked for a count.

cards.name: Entertainment Token
cards.title: Token
cards.text: An Entertainment token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: Struck last of the eight, because Entertainment was the last study the borough admitted it had. Oatmeal was handed the first one on a stage, which is exactly where he would have chosen to be handed it.

cards.name: Building Token
cards.title: Token
cards.text: A Building token. Held beside your Supply and spent by the cards that call for it; never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck.
cards.flavor: A surveyor’s chit, issued when a roof goes on and kept by the Mayor who raised it. Barrow has more of them than anyone in the borough and keeps them in the tin his father kept nails in.

cards.name: Barrow's Measure
cards.text: Requires Barrow and a Crafts Character. Gain 2 Supply, and the next Building you buy costs 1 less Supply.
cards.flavor: He walks the lot before the auction, on his own, and comes back with a figure. The Capital City has never yet asked less than the figure and has never once been more than a Supply above it.

cards.name: Biff's Beat
cards.text: Requires Biff. One of your opponent's Characters turns one step back toward Busy, then you may rehire a Character from your Unemployment for 1 less Supply.
cards.flavor: The trouble stops, because Biff is immovable and it does. Then he walks them home, and a week later he has found them something to do. Both halves of that are the job; he has given up explaining which is the important one.

cards.name: Rosabeth's Rounds
cards.text: Requires Rosabeth and an Agriculture Character. Rehire an Agriculture Character from your Unemployment for free, then draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: She does the beds first and the borough second, and by the time she has got round to the second half of it somebody has been on the beds a fortnight and is fit to be somewhere else.

cards.name: Oatmeal's Benefit Night
cards.text: Requires Oatmeal and an Entertainment Character. Draw 2 cards and gain 2 Supply. Your opponent gains 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Whatever the hall takes goes to whoever needs it, and Oatmeal has never once checked which town they were from before handing it over. Four of his brothers and sisters at the back, as always.

cards.name: Copper's Stocktake
cards.text: Requires Copper and a Commerce Character. Look at the top three cards of your deck and send any of them to your Town Dump, then gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Everything out, everything weighed, everything written down, and the half of it that was never going to be any use carried out to the yard. He does it twice a year and is cheerful for a week afterwards.

cards.name: Warren Muster
cards.text: Requires two Rabbits. Recruit a Character costing 2 or less from your hand for free; it enters upright.
cards.flavor: Two rabbits is a conversation. Two rabbits and a notice on the Lending Library door is nine of them on the step by Thursday, and one of them already holding a tool.

cards.name: The Night Round
cards.text: Requires two Owls. Two of your Characters each turn one step toward upright, then look at the top two cards of your deck and put any of them on the bottom.
cards.flavor: Bean opens the counter, Hoot does the doors, Barnaby is already at the ledger. By the time the rest of the borough is up, the night has quietly put half of tomorrow in order.

cards.name: The Bins at Dawn
cards.text: Requires a Raccoon. Take a card from the City Dump, then draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Hazel is back before the lamps go out, with something the Capital City threw away and a straight face about where it came from. It is always exactly the thing the borough needed and nobody asks.

cards.name: Guild Night
cards.text: Requires two Crafts Characters. Ready one of your Characters and draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: The bench gets cleared, the good chairs come out, and whatever anyone is stuck on goes round the table once. Berry says nothing for an hour and then says the thing that fixes it.

cards.name: A Lecture at the Hall
cards.text: Requires two Science Characters. Draw 2 cards, and your next Event needs one fewer Character.
cards.flavor: Comet asks the question everyone else had decided not to ask, twice, and is not embarrassed either time. Half the hall leaves knowing something; the other half leaves knowing what to look up.

cards.name: Ledger Day
cards.text: Requires two Commerce Characters. Gain 4 Supply and draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Quarter day. Half the borough’s accounts pass over Peanut’s counter between orders, and everybody who comes in for a cup leaves knowing something they did not know about what things cost.

cards.name: Barrow's Yard
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, the next Building you buy this turn costs 1 less Supply.
cards.flavor: Stone stacked by size, the good sand under a tarpaulin, and a Badger who will tell you what a wall is worth whether or not you have asked. He bids on every lot that comes up with a roof on it.

cards.name: The Warren
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, if you control a Rabbit, draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Nobody built it and nobody can say how far back it goes. Clover’s family came out of one end of it and Lynnette’s press sits over the other, and on any given morning there are more rabbits in it than were in it last night.

cards.name: The Observatory Steps
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, if you control a Science Character, look at the top two cards of your deck and put any of them on the bottom, then gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Inkwell swept them for a season to be allowed up them and Comet read every book at the top before the board would look at her. Whoever is on the steps at four in the morning knows what is coming before the borough does.

cards.name: The Counting House
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: Whenever one of your Characters finishes a shift, if you control a Commerce Character, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: A long desk, two lamps and the borough’s quarterly returns in order of age. Copper weighs what comes in and Peanut works out what it was worth, usually between orders and usually before being asked.

cards.name: The Quill Wall
cards.title: Town Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, one of your Characters cannot be targeted by your opponent until your next turn, and your Characters cannot be sent to Unemployment by an effect this turn.
cards.flavor: Bob leans on it, Biff walks past it four times a night, and Berry mended the gate in it twice without being asked. It is not much of a wall. Nothing has ever got over it.

cards.name: The Guild Hall
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, if you control a Crafts Character, one of your Characters turns one step toward upright and you gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: The engine course runs here twice a year and Comet took it twice. Barrow will not join and turns up anyway, on the grounds that somebody has to tell them about foundations.

cards.name: The Long Room
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, if you control a Lore Character, look at the top two cards of your deck and put any of them on the bottom, then gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: The Lending Library’s upper floor, where the ribbons live and the reading lamps are never all out. Inkwell has a chair in it that everybody knows is theirs and nobody has ever said so out loud.

cards.name: Maribel
cards.title: Seed Keeper
cards.text: When Maribel is recruited, your next Event needs one fewer Character.
cards.flavor: She was six, the oak was two hundred, and the grange argued over her head for a day and a half before it gave in. The oak is still there.

cards.name: Maribel
cards.title: Seed Bank Clerk
cards.text: Upgrades Maribel. When Maribel completes a shift, you may return an Event from your Town Dump to your hand.
cards.flavor: Thrown out on the Friday, filed again on the Monday, in her handwriting, with the date of the hedge on it.

cards.name: Maribel
cards.title: Seed Vault Scientist
cards.text: Upgrades Maribel. The first Event you play each turn that requires Science lets you draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Every variety the borough has ever grown, dried, doubled and labelled twice, against a year nobody has had yet.

cards.name: Maribel
cards.title: Horticulturist
cards.text: Upgrades Maribel. The first Event you play each turn lets you draw 1 card, and if you control three Buildings or fewer, gain 1 Supply as well.
cards.flavor: She would rather the town grew slowly and kept what it had, and she will say so, at length, in writing, on the record.

cards.name: Maribel
cards.title: Seed Bank Director
cards.text: Upgrades Maribel. Once per turn, an Event you play requires one fewer Character. (This does not stack with the Statue of Ingenuity.)
cards.flavor: The objection the town threw out three seasons ago, back on the table, word for word, with the seed stock to prove it.

cards.name: Maribel
cards.title: Seed Sorter
cards.text: A short shift: 1 turn, 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Trays, tweezers, and one variety at a time until the light goes. Maribel was doing this before the borough thought of it as a seed bank, and she is the reason it became one.

cards.name: Beck
cards.title: Bylaw Reader
cards.text: A long shift: 3 turns, then 1 Supply. When Beck completes a shift, draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Three days on the ward roll, and not one animal in the office could tell you what he thought of any of it.

cards.name: Beck
cards.title: Ward Clerk
cards.text: When Beck completes a shift, you may return an Event from your Town Dump to your hand.
cards.flavor: He had read the minutes nobody had wanted since the bridge went, so he knew the answer, and waited to be asked twice.

cards.name: Beck
cards.title: Lamplighter’s Clerk
cards.text: Upgrades Beck. When Beck becomes upright, take a Market card from the City Dump and gain it.
cards.flavor: The lamps are logged by seven and he is home by half past, with somebody's water-stained novel out of the City Dump under one arm.

cards.name: Beck
cards.title: Keeper of the Ward Book
cards.text: Upgrades Beck. Your challenge bids win ties. When Beck completes a shift, you may return an Event from your Town Dump to your hand.
cards.flavor: Fifteen years of evenings, a candle at a time, and now there is nothing in the book he has not read — which is why the room goes quiet when he finally says something.

cards.name: Beck
cards.title: Candlelight Reader
cards.text: Upgrades Beck. The first Event you play each turn that requires Lore lets you take a card from the City Dump.
cards.flavor: Split almanacs, water-stained novels, ward minutes nobody has wanted since the bridge went — Beck has read all of it by candle, and knows which heap the thing you need went out on. Annabelle keeps the ones with words; Beck gets first read.

cards.name: Beck Reads by Candlelight
cards.text: Requires Beck. Draw 2 cards. The next Event you play this turn requires one fewer Character.
cards.flavor: One candle, one chair, two hours, and by morning he knows the clause the rest of the ward is about to need.

cards.name: Marmalade
cards.title: Night Baker
cards.text: A patient shift: 2 turns, then 2 Supply. When Marmalade completes a shift, your Characters advance an extra step at your next Ready.
cards.flavor: The ovens are banked at eleven and the shapes start about one: a hedgehog loaf, twice, because the first one came out looking like Bob.

cards.name: Marmalade
cards.title: Dough Kneader
cards.text: When Marmalade is recruited, your Characters advance an extra step at your next Ready.
cards.flavor: Somebody put a bowl in front of a horrible kitten to keep his paws busy, and the borough has been quieter ever since.

cards.name: Marmalade
cards.title: Market Baker
cards.text: Upgrades Marmalade. When Marmalade is recruited, gain 1 Supply and your Characters advance an extra step at your next Ready.
cards.flavor: He cannot keep a queue moving to save his life, because everybody in it has something to tell him, and he listens to all of it.

cards.name: Marmalade
cards.title: Neighborhood Baker
cards.text: Upgrades Marmalade. When Marmalade becomes upright, you may feed a Character costing 2 or less in your Unemployment; it comes back to work Busy, for nothing.
cards.flavor: The tray goes round the kittens first and is empty before anybody has paid for anything. He knows exactly what a kitten with nothing to do turns into.

cards.name: Marmalade
cards.title: Harvest Head Baker
cards.text: Upgrades Marmalade. The first shift you complete each turn produces 1 extra Supply. Busy, once per game: Marmalade readies himself.
cards.flavor: Harvest week, three ovens, six recipes nobody asked for, and a cat who has not been where he was rostered since he was a kitten.

cards.name: Marmalade
cards.title: Oven Keeper
cards.text: Upgrades Marmalade. At the start of your turn, if you control another Cat, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: The ovens are banked overnight and shared out by morning, and Marmalade is who banks them. The kittens are served first and usually before it is paid for — which is why, in a town with cats in it, Marmalade's morning is never short.

cards.name: Mittens
cards.title: Rooftop Cat
cards.text: Hired from the Capital City; enters Busy. When Mittens becomes upright, look at the top two cards of your deck and put them back in any order. Busy, once per game: Mittens readies itself.
cards.flavor: Nobody hired it, exactly. It was on the ridge above the yard, it said one sentence about the hinge, and the Hiring Hall wrote a name on the line because somebody had to.

cards.name: Morty
cards.title: Mill Kitchen Cook
cards.text: When Morty is recruited, your town braces: the next shared shock passes it over.
cards.flavor: He grinds it and then he cooks it, and the animals who bring grain to the mill have learned to turn up hungry.

cards.name: Morty
cards.title: Watermill Mechanic
cards.text: When Morty becomes upright, you may rehire a Character from your Unemployment for 2 less Supply.
cards.flavor: Taken apart twice this week because it was very nearly right, and he can always use a pair of paws on the other end of it.

cards.name: Morty
cards.title: Steam Engineer
cards.text: Upgrades Morty. When Morty becomes upright, your town braces: the next shared shock passes it over.
cards.flavor: The Science hall said the boiler would not hold. Morty built it anyway, invited the hall to lunch beside it, and the borough has sheltered behind that boiler twice since.

cards.name: Morty
cards.title: Master Millwright
cards.text: Upgrades Morty. The first shift you complete each turn produces 1 extra Supply.
cards.flavor: Every gear in the borough turns a little truer once Morty has had a look at it, and there is always somebody eating at the end of the mill while he does.

cards.name: Morty
cards.title: Grain Miller
cards.text: Upgrades Morty. A steady shift: 2 turns, 3 Supply.
cards.flavor: Before the kitchen, before the boiler, the plain half of the mill: sacks in, stones dressed, flour out, all day. Morty will tell you it is the only part of the job that has never once gone wrong.

cards.name: Morty’s Boiler Test
cards.text: Requires Morty. Gain 2 Supply. Your town braces: the next shared shock passes it over.
cards.flavor: Everybody behind the wall, please. No, further. Right — and there's a pot on afterwards, so don't go home.

cards.name: Moss
cards.title: Ploughwright
cards.text: When Moss is recruited, your town braces: the next shared shock passes it over.
cards.flavor: The hitch is not on any drawing and has never once fouled, which is the whole of Moss in one bent piece of iron.

cards.name: Moss
cards.title: Toolsmith
cards.text: When Moss completes a shift, Buildings cost you 1 less until your next turn.
cards.flavor: Half the workshop uses his bench jig and not one of them knows whose it was, which suits him exactly.

cards.name: Moss
cards.title: Guild Architect
cards.text: When Moss becomes upright, you may rehire a Character from your Unemployment for 2 less Supply.
cards.flavor: Two commissions lost and one formal warning, and he still takes the apprentice nobody else will have.

cards.name: Moss
cards.title: Rocketwright
cards.text: Upgrades Moss. When Moss becomes upright, if you control Comet, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Comet asked for more boom. Moss read the drawing, put it down, and has notes.

cards.name: Moss
cards.title: Bridgewright
cards.text: Upgrades Moss. Busy: ready one of your Characters.
cards.flavor: A third lighter than the drawing, refused twice by the guild, and standing over the river these eleven years while the drawing sits in a drawer.

cards.name: Moss
cards.title: Timber Hand
cards.text: A short shift: 1 turn, 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Berry taught him at twelve; this is Moss at eleven, stacking other animals' timber and already stacking it his own way. Nobody had yet had to write him a warning about it.

cards.name: Moss's Rehiring Day
cards.text: Requires Moss. Rehire a Character from your Unemployment for free; it enters upright.
cards.flavor: Every old apprentice's apron still on its hook, including the two the guild told him not to take on.

cards.name: Daniel
cards.title: Ink Mixer
cards.text: A long shift: 3 turns, then 1 Supply. When Daniel is recruited, your next Event needs one fewer Character.
cards.flavor: Three days grinding oak gall for a colour that will only ever be used for roads they will not take.

cards.name: Daniel
cards.title: Canal Cartographer
cards.text: When Daniel is recruited, your next Event needs one fewer Character. When Daniel becomes upright, look at the top two cards of your deck and put them back in any order.
cards.flavor: Charted to the county line from the ferry steps, off two hours of debriefing a lighterman and not one step of towpath.

cards.name: Daniel
cards.title: Star Charter
cards.text: Upgrades Daniel. Busy: the next Event you play requires one fewer Character.
cards.flavor: The one journey nobody can take anyway, charted from a window with the door shut, which is Daniel's idea of a perfect night.

cards.name: Daniel
cards.title: Master Cartographer
cards.text: Upgrades Daniel. When Daniel becomes upright, look at the top three cards of your deck and put them back in any order, then look at the top two cards of the Market Deck.
cards.flavor: Every apprentice sent somewhere they have never been goes with a sheet in their paw in a mouse's careful hand — and every one of them has been further than the mouse.

cards.name: Daniel
cards.title: Chart Copier
cards.text: Upgrades Daniel. A short shift: 1 turn, 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Somebody else's survey, traced true, four times over so that four animals can carry one. Daniel has copied more of the borough than he has walked, which is most of it.

cards.name: Ned
cards.title: Page Runner
cards.text: When Ned completes a shift, put 1 Supply by on Ned.
cards.flavor: Every errand logged, every log dated, and the dates are why the far hedgerow argument took an afternoon instead of a season.

cards.name: Ned
cards.title: Night Archivist
cards.text: Upgrades Ned. When Ned becomes upright, look at the top two cards of your deck and put them back in any order.
cards.flavor: 'That is close, and it is not what happened.' Said levelly, at eleven at night, to an empty room and a wrong shelf.

cards.name: Ned
cards.title: Reference Librarian
cards.text: Upgrades Ned. When Ned becomes upright, look at the top three cards of your deck and put them back in any order. When Ned completes a shift, put 1 Supply by on Ned.
cards.flavor: They will not paraphrase it for you. They will hand you the book, open, at the page, and wait.

cards.name: Ned
cards.title: Chancellor of Records
cards.text: Upgrades Ned. Busy: take every Supply your Characters have put by.
cards.flavor: A year of saying nothing, and then the whole discrepancy at once — in order, with the dates, and no correction ever printed.

cards.name: Ned
cards.title: Ward Recorder
cards.text: Upgrades Ned. The first Event you play each turn that requires Civics lets you draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Both of the borough's standing arguments about the far hedgerow were settled out of Ned's shelves in an afternoon. Whatever the ward is about to do, Ned has the last time it did it, in a box, labelled.

cards.name: Daisy
cards.title: Petal Sweeper
cards.text: When Daisy completes a shift, put 1 Supply by on Daisy.
cards.flavor: Swept up at closing and dried on the rack over the door, because a squirrel does not throw away anything that will keep.

cards.name: Daisy
cards.title: Bouquet Weaver
cards.text: When Daisy is recruited, she and one other Character you control work together: while both are in your town, each of their shifts pays 1 more Supply.
cards.flavor: She can tell you what the posy is saying and what the animal who ordered it thinks it is saying, and she is never wrong twice.

cards.name: Daisy
cards.title: Night-Bloom Florist
cards.text: Upgrades Daisy. When Daisy completes a shift, put 2 Supply by on Daisy.
cards.flavor: The stock that only opens after dark, cut at two in the morning, for a wedding she is not in.

cards.name: Daisy
cards.title: Festival Florist
cards.text: Upgrades Daisy. Busy: take every Supply your Characters have put by.
cards.flavor: Four days, every garland on the square, no sleep, and a year's takings taken in one go — which is how a squirrel likes to be paid, and how she likes to be surprised.

cards.name: Peter
cards.title: Hedge Cutter
cards.text: A short shift: 1 turn, 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Peter is given the billhook and the near end of the field, and told to keep up. He does keep up. Nobody has yet mentioned that he is doing it correctly.

cards.name: Peter
cards.title: Hedgelayer
cards.text: Upgrades Peter. A steady shift: 2 turns, 4 Supply.
cards.flavor: Cut it most of the way through, bend it over while it is still alive, peg it down and wait fifteen years to find out whether you were any good. Peter has been good for eleven of them so far.

cards.name: Osh
cards.title: Sharpener's Boy
cards.text: A short shift: 1 turn, 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: He is not yet allowed the wheel. He is allowed to carry the wheel, which at his size is the harder half of the job.

cards.name: Osh
cards.title: Edge Grinder
cards.text: Upgrades Osh. A steady shift: 2 turns, 3 Supply.
cards.flavor: Eleven days, the same order every time, and at the end of it every edge in the borough is the same edge again. Osh could tell you whose shears these are with his eyes shut, and has.

cards.name: Adam
cards.title: Road Mender
cards.text: A short shift: 1 turn, 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Barrow, rake, hot stuff out of the pot, and the square's cobbles back down before the stalls come at six. Adam has never been thanked for this and has never expected to be.

cards.name: Adam
cards.title: Surveyor of Ways
cards.text: Upgrades Adam. A steady shift: 2 turns, 5 Supply.
cards.flavor: The long pull to the county gate was his idea, and it is a quarter-hour shorter than the one it replaced. He got carts round the whole of that spring the bridge was down, and he will tell you it was nothing much, at length.

cards.name: Cassadee
cards.title: Stage Hand
cards.text: A short shift: 1 turn, 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Chairs in, chairs out, lamp trimmed, and one hedgehog at the back holding a list nobody else has read. She was fourteen and it was already her list.

cards.name: Cassadee
cards.title: Hall Manager
cards.text: Upgrades Cassadee. A steady shift: 2 turns, 4 Supply.
cards.flavor: The room, the lamp oil, the running order and the chairs away by midnight. Cassadee has never once been on the stage and the evening has never once started without her.

cards.name: Annabelle
cards.title: Paper Sorter
cards.text: A short shift: 1 turn, 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Wet paper, cold paws, and a stack by the gate that will be a shelf by the autumn. Annabelle has read most of the borough's rubbish and remembers an unfair amount of it.

cards.name: Annabelle
cards.title: Salvage Archivist
cards.text: Upgrades Annabelle. A steady shift: 2 turns, 4 Supply.
cards.flavor: Flattened, dried, labelled and shelved: a year of Grain Exchange returns that exist nowhere else because the Grain Exchange threw its own copy out. She has been wrong before, so she keeps the illegible ones too.

cards.name: Liz
cards.title: Scale Hand
cards.text: A short shift: 1 turn, 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: She chocks the wheels, waits for the beam, and calls the figure up to the office. It has been the right figure every time, which at the Grain Exchange is not nothing.

cards.name: Liz
cards.title: Weighbridge Keeper
cards.text: Upgrades Liz. A steady shift: 2 turns, 5 Supply.
cards.flavor: Every loaded cart in the borough crosses Liz's plate and is paid on what she writes. Copper certifies the bridge each spring and has never had to move it a hair. She reads the carter's face anyway, out of habit.

cards.name: Taco
cards.title: Cart Cook
cards.text: A short shift: 1 turn, 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: One pan, one lamp, and whatever came off the last boat. Taco learned to cook standing up on a moving cart and has never seen the appeal of doing it any other way.

cards.name: Taco
cards.title: Quayside Cook
cards.text: Upgrades Taco. A steady shift: 2 turns, 4 Supply.
cards.flavor: Shut at noon, open at four in the morning, and never twice in the same place. The lightermen find him every time and not one of them can tell you how.

cards.name: Cookie
cards.title: Biscuit Maker
cards.text: A short shift: 1 turn, 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Hard biscuit, twice through the oven, on the last of the heat. It is not very nice and it will still be there in March, which is the whole idea.

cards.name: Cookie
cards.title: Winter Stores Cook
cards.text: Upgrades Cookie. A steady shift: 2 turns, 4 Supply.
cards.flavor: The late heat after the bread is out, and shelves that do not get opened until the weather turns. Cookie has never eaten anything in the year she baked it and does not intend to start.

cards.name: Sota
cards.title: Lens Grinder
cards.text: A short shift: 1 turn, 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Months on one blank, and the last of it done by feel at about the speed of a plant growing. Sota can tell you the figure is out before the test says so.

cards.name: Sota
cards.title: Telescope Fitter
cards.text: Upgrades Sota. A steady shift: 2 turns, 4 Supply.
cards.flavor: Every small instrument in the Observatory came off Sota's bench, and the two big ones have been re-seated by them twice. They have looked through exactly as many of them as politeness required.

cards.name: Andrew
cards.title: Night Copyist
cards.text: A short shift: 1 turn, 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: A page or two a night, in a hand so even the Library has twice filed his copy as the original. Andrew has never pointed this out.

cards.name: Andrew
cards.title: Keeper of the Late Desk
cards.text: Upgrades Andrew. A steady shift: 2 turns, 3 Supply.
cards.flavor: He locks the door behind Inkwell's evening and then does not leave. The Counting House has asked twice what exactly it is paying for, and the Library has given up trying to explain.

cards.name: Orien
cards.title: Tally Clerk
cards.text: When Orien completes a shift, your next recruit costs 1 less Supply.
cards.flavor: His first paid week, and he came home with a table of every price the Capital City took that season, in four colours, for nobody. The borough has been quietly using it ever since.

cards.name: Orien
cards.title: Rate Checker
cards.text: Upgrades Orien. When you announce a purchase, your challenges cost 1 less Supply until the end of your turn.
cards.flavor: He has read the lot, the four lots before it and what all five went for last year. You are not bidding against the room; you are bidding against his margin, and he has already worked out where it is.

cards.name: Orien
cards.title: Borough Actuary
cards.text: Upgrades Orien. Busy: your next Building costs 1 less Supply.
cards.flavor: Ask him what the next Building will go for and he tells you, and he is within a Supply, and he is a little put out that you sounded surprised.

cards.name: Orien
cards.title: Survey Computer
cards.text: Upgrades Orien. While Orien is upright, every shift your Characters complete pays 1 more Supply.
cards.flavor: The machine in his back room is on its fourth rebuild, half Observatory cast-offs and half whatever Patch would sell him, and it clicks all night. It is also why he is never at the bonfire.

cards.name: Orien
cards.title: Town Planner
cards.text: Upgrades Orien. When Orien becomes upright, your next recruit costs 2 less Supply.
cards.flavor: Eleven committees have made him their figures badger and not one has asked him to speak. He likes it best when the room goes quiet and looks at him, and he can put the number on the table and go home.

cards.name: Patch
cards.title: Junkyard Diver
cards.text: When Patch completes a shift, your next Building costs 1 less Supply.
cards.flavor: Small enough to get under things, quick enough to get out again. There was money in it and no plan beyond it, and for about two years that was the whole business.

cards.name: Patch
cards.title: Salvage Sorter
cards.text: Upgrades Patch. When Patch is recruited, your next Building costs 1 less Supply.
cards.flavor: He put a new roller in a mangle and sold it back to the animal who had thrown it out, for more than it cost new. Standing there with the coin, he worked out that the diving was the least interesting part of it.

cards.name: Patch
cards.title: Valuer
cards.text: Upgrades Patch. Busy: take a Market card from the City Dump and gain it.
cards.flavor: They bring him a thing and ask whether it is worth keeping. He turns it over twice and tells them. Then they start bringing him leases, and seasons that have not gone well, and he turns those over twice too.

cards.name: Patch
cards.title: Yard Foreman
cards.text: Upgrades Patch. When Patch completes a shift, take a Market card from the City Dump and gain it.
cards.flavor: Out, sorted, mended, improved, sold back at a price nobody has ever complained about. Annabelle takes the paper. The two of them have never once discussed it.

cards.name: Patch
cards.title: Reclamation Merchant
