cards.text: Upgrades Patch. Busy: pull one of your Buildings down and put a Building from the City Dump up in its place, then your next Building costs 1 less Supply.
cards.flavor: He will tell you he is only a raccoon with a yard, and then tell you to keep the lease and sell the cart. You will, and it will have been the right way round.

cards.name: Patch's Second Opinion
cards.text: Requires Patch. Take a Market card from the City Dump and gain it.
cards.flavor: You came about the cart. He has looked at the cart, and at you, and he is going to start with the lease.

cards.name: Pebble
cards.title: Crossing Hand
cards.text: When Pebble completes a shift, take an Otter token.
cards.flavor: Four crossings an hour, the same rope, the same eleven regulars and their eleven opinions. One worn wooden otter into the tin for each of them, the way their great-grandmother struck them.

cards.name: Pebble
cards.title: Bridge Courier
cards.text: When Pebble is recruited, take an Otter token, and another Character you control is upright at the start of your next turn.
cards.flavor: Half the borough has one of the ferry's chits in a pocket they never handed back. Pebble has never once asked for one of them.

cards.name: Pebble
cards.title: Ferry Master
cards.text: Upgrades Pebble. Busy: move a shift from one of your Characters to another, then take an Otter token.
cards.flavor: Brooke has asked them twice why they are not climbing out of this. Standing where your father stood, Pebble said, with his grandmother's chits still in the tin, is not a thing you climb out of.

cards.name: Pebble
cards.title: Harbour Warden
cards.text: Upgrades Pebble. At the end of your turn, take an Otter token for each of your Characters who stood up this turn. When Pebble becomes upright, if you hold at least three Otter tokens, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Willow asked three times. Pebble took it on the third and only on terms: the post, the office, the whole harbour if you like — and the boat, four crossings an hour, every morning, as before.

cards.name: Scott
cards.title: Story Collector
cards.text: When Scott completes a shift, put 2 Supply by on Scott, then look at the top card of the Market Deck.
cards.flavor: Every market between here and the Capital City, every lighterman off a night run, every old animal on a bench. He takes the story and pays for it with a better one, and most of it goes in the tin for years.

cards.name: Scott
cards.title: Pamphleteer
cards.text: Upgrades Scott. When Scott becomes upright, look at the top 3 cards of your deck and put them back in any order.
cards.flavor: Dragons under the far hedgerow on one shelf and the true account of 1841 on the next, and he will not be drawn on which of them sells better. He orders a run the way he orders a page.

cards.name: Scott
cards.title: Town Chronicler
cards.text: Upgrades Scott. When Scott becomes upright, look at the top 3 cards of your deck and put them back in any order, then look at the top card of the Market Deck.
cards.flavor: Everything about a real animal or a real year goes across Ned's shelves first, and Ned certifies it or Scott cuts it. Fifteen years, and Lynnette has never printed a correction to a word of his.

cards.name: Scott
cards.title: Natural Historian
cards.text: Upgrades Scott. When Scott becomes upright, look at the top 3 cards of your deck and put them back in any order, then put 2 Supply by on Scott.
cards.flavor: He goes out after the things nobody has written down yet, on the grounds that a thing nobody has written down is either a discovery or a very good lie, and he has a use for both.

cards.name: Scott
cards.title: Author of the Boroughs
cards.text: Upgrades Scott. When Scott becomes upright, take every Supply your Characters have put by, then look at the top two cards of the Market Deck.
cards.flavor: A season finally calls for it, and he opens the tin, and it turns out he has had the answer filed since about a decade ago. There is a fart joke on page four. There is always a fart joke on page four.

cards.name: Scott's Reading Hour
cards.text: Requires Scott. Limited 2: at the start of your turn, draw 1 card and look at the top card of the Market Deck.
cards.flavor: He reads the boundary dispute out in full, with the dates, and puts the joke about somebody's uncle exactly where the room starts to go. The little ones are waiting for page four and he knows it.

cards.name: Lindsay
cards.title: Potting Helper
cards.text: When Lindsay completes a shift, gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Can held at exactly the right height for exactly the right count, eyes somewhere past the roof glass. Ask her afterwards what she did and she cannot tell you. Ask the pots and they can.

cards.name: Lindsay
cards.title: Glasshouse Hand
cards.text: Upgrades Lindsay. At the start of your turn, if you control an Agriculture Character, gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: She has been overheard costing out a glasshouse on the moon and settling an argument nobody was having about whether rain smells before or after it lands. Meanwhile the bench came in over again.

cards.name: Lindsay
cards.title: Herb Grower
cards.text: Upgrades Lindsay. Busy, once per game: Lindsay readies herself.
cards.flavor: Marmalade will not use anybody else's rosemary. She cut it for him this morning without noticing that she had got up, gone out, or come back.

cards.name: Lindsay
cards.title: Conservatory Keeper
cards.text: Upgrades Lindsay. At the start of your turn, every shift your Characters complete this turn pays 1 more Supply.
cards.flavor: Her beds come in over. Always, every year, more than the row should give. Orien's figures on the glasshouse have a note in the margin that just says 'ask her again in spring'.

cards.name: Lindsay
cards.title: Moon Gardener
cards.text: Upgrades Lindsay. At the start of your turn, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Twenty years of not paying attention, and it turns out this is where she was. Comet, who was turned down twice for wanting the moon too openly, likes her enormously.

cards.name: Pockets
cards.title: Kerbside Dealer
cards.text: When Pockets completes a shift, you may return an Event from your Town Dump to your hand.
cards.flavor: He taught Patch to dive. He leads with that. It has been getting steadily less useful to him for about fifteen years.

cards.name: Pockets
cards.title: Odd-Lot Dealer
cards.text: Upgrades Pockets. When Pockets is recruited, take a Market card from the City Dump and gain it, and you may take an Event out of your opponent's Town Dump into your hand.
cards.flavor: Patch sells you back your own mangle, mended. Pockets sells you somebody else's and does not say whose. Nothing he does is quite a crime; several things are the shape of one, seen from a distance, in poor light.

cards.name: Pockets
cards.title: Salvage Raccoon
cards.text: Hired from the Capital City; enters Busy. Busy: take a Market card from the City Dump and gain it.
cards.flavor: The borough hires him when it wants back a thing it has already thrown away. It is careful not to ask how, and it pays him in the same careful way.

cards.name: Hibiscus
cards.title: Post Runner
cards.text: When Hibiscus is recruited, another Character you control is upright at the start of your next turn.
cards.flavor: Handover at the sorting bench at five, and that is the only part of the day Hibiscus does quickly. After that it is doors.

cards.name: Hibiscus
cards.title: Night Mail
cards.text: Upgrades Hibiscus. When Hibiscus becomes upright, another Character you control is upright at the start of your next turn.
cards.flavor: The second post goes out at ten at night because the first one took until eight, and every lit window on the lane gets a wave whether it wants one or not.

cards.name: Hibiscus
cards.title: Round Walker
cards.text: Upgrades Hibiscus. When Hibiscus completes a shift, another Character you control is upright at the start of your next turn.
cards.flavor: Four hours of round in seven hours, because a bunny who genuinely wants to know how your mother is cannot be got off a doorstep in under ten minutes, and they genuinely want to know, at every door, every day.

cards.name: Hibiscus
cards.title: Mail Coach Driver
cards.text: Upgrades Hibiscus. The first time you announce a purchase each turn, another Character you control is upright at the start of your next turn.
cards.flavor: The coach leaves on the hour whether the passengers are aboard or not, which is the one hour of the week Hibiscus is on time, and they consider it a kindness rather than a rule.

cards.name: Hibiscus
cards.title: Postmaster
cards.text: Upgrades Hibiscus. When Hibiscus becomes upright, one of your other Characters becomes upright.
cards.flavor: Biff walks his beat to stop the trouble. Hibiscus walks theirs and the trouble never starts, and by nine the whole lane is out of doors with its apron on and an opinion about the ferry.

cards.name: Hibiscus's Post Route
cards.text: Requires Hibiscus. Gain 2 Supply, then one of your Characters is upright at the start of your next turn.
cards.flavor: Rain, snow or bidding war, the post gets through — late, and with the whole lane standing in its doorways behind it.

cards.name: Quill
cards.title: Orchard Hand
cards.text: When Quill is recruited, one of your Characters cannot be targeted by your opponent until your next turn.
cards.flavor: She grew up under the rows, in the long grass, being handed up windfalls. Nothing has ever reached anybody in that grass and she does not intend to be the generation it starts with.

cards.name: Quill
cards.title: Orchard Keeper
cards.text: Upgrades Quill. While Quill is in town, your Characters cannot be sent to Unemployment by an effect.
cards.flavor: A third of the animals who turned up for one Saturday were still there at the end of the week, on the books, being paid. She has never once said so out loud.

cards.name: Quill
cards.title: Cider Maker
cards.text: Upgrades Quill. When Quill becomes upright, gain 1 Supply and one of your other Characters cannot be targeted by your opponent until your next turn.
cards.flavor: The social runs in the barn from September to about February, and the bonfires happen whenever the prunings get above knee height, which is considerably more often than pruning requires. She invents reasons.

cards.name: Quill
cards.title: Orchard Scribe
cards.text: Upgrades Quill. Busy: your Characters cannot be sent to Unemployment by an effect until your next turn, and you draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: The book says which tree fruited when, going back three keepers. It also says who picked, which is not what the book is for, and is the only record in the borough of a good few animals' worst autumns.

cards.name: Quill
cards.title: Harvest Steward
cards.text: Upgrades Quill. When Quill becomes upright, one of your other Characters cannot be targeted by your opponent and your Characters cannot be sent to Unemployment by an effect until your next turn.
cards.flavor: The Hiring Hall sends them and pretends it hasn't; Quill takes them and pretends she hasn't noticed. She hands over a basket, asks whether they can carry a ladder, and puts the kettle on for thirty.

cards.name: Quinn
cards.title: Meeting Scribe
cards.text: When Quinn completes a shift, you may rehire a Character from your Unemployment for 1 less Supply.
cards.flavor: At the back of the ward meeting with the book open, saying nothing. Two or three of the older animals will not sit with their backs to him.

cards.name: Quinn
cards.title: Town Scrivener
cards.text: Hired from the Capital City; enters Busy. When Quinn becomes upright, you may return an Event from your Town Dump to your hand.
cards.flavor: The children are settled on it: he is a mage, because the writing comes out faster than the talking goes in, and because he was at the fair, the regatta and the Hiring Hall on one afternoon.

cards.name: Quinn
cards.title: Keeper of the Record
cards.text: Upgrades Quinn. When Quinn becomes upright, you may rehire a Character from your Unemployment for free.
cards.flavor: He turns back four years, finds the animal who did that exact work in a bad winter and has not been asked since, writes the name on a slip, hands it over, and says nothing. It has put more animals back to work than any committee sitting.

cards.name: Roger
cards.title: Locksmith
cards.text: Whenever a bid of yours is tied, gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: The lock, the lease, the rota, the argument between the two carters — and all of it on the way to somewhere else. He cuts a key for every door in town and keeps a spare for none of them.

cards.name: Roger
cards.title: Records Clerk
cards.text: Upgrades Roger. When you announce a purchase, look at the top 2 cards of the Market Deck.
cards.flavor: Chair, warden, clerk, judge — every one of them handed to him by a room turning round and looking at him, and this was the first. He was twenty-two and had only mentioned that the figures were out.

cards.name: Roger
cards.title: Circuit Judge
cards.text: Upgrades Roger. Whenever a bid of yours is tied, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: He has adjourned a hearing for a week to think about it. He has found for both sides in writing, twice, which Ned had to file as two documents.

cards.name: Roger
cards.title: Fair Broker
cards.text: Upgrades Roger. Whenever a bid of yours is tied, toss Roger's ha'penny: heads, raise one of your open bids by 2; tails, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Somebody else calls it in the air. He has never called it himself, not once, on the grounds that calling it would be taking a side.

cards.name: Roger
cards.title: Ombudsman
cards.text: Upgrades Roger. Your challenge bids win ties. Whenever a bid of yours is tied, gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: The ha'penny is worn almost smooth. It has settled four boundary questions, a dispute about a bandstand and who was to have the good pitch at the fair, and the borough considers all four settled forever.

cards.name: Earl
cards.title: Tea Boy
cards.text: When Earl is recruited, your next recruit costs 1 less Supply, or 2 less if it upgrades a Character you already have.
cards.flavor: He carried trays before he kept anything, and he was already at it then: nobody got a cup off that tray without also getting told what they ought to be doing next.

cards.name: Earl
cards.title: Tea Trader
cards.text: Upgrades Earl. When Earl completes a shift, your next recruit costs 1 less Supply if it upgrades a Character you already have.
cards.flavor: There is always a spare cup behind the counter and it is never free, exactly: you pay for it by hearing what he thinks you should be doing by spring.

cards.name: Earl
cards.title: Coffee Roaster
cards.text: Upgrades Earl. When Earl completes a shift, toss for it: heads, your next recruit costs 2 less Supply if it upgrades a Character you already have; tails, gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: This is Earl before the first cup: four in the morning, the urn in one paw, three steps too many in the plan. When it is an even call whether an animal is ready, this is the Earl who leans on it.

cards.name: Earl
cards.title: Tea House Keeper
cards.text: Upgrades Earl. When Earl becomes upright, your next recruit costs 2 less Supply if it upgrades a Character you already have.
cards.flavor: Bean has the mornings and the accounts. Earl has the long afternoons, when an animal who needs to sit down with somebody sits down for two hours and goes away having agreed to something.

cards.name: Statue of Kindness
cards.text: On gain: feed a Character costing 1 or less in your Unemployment; it comes back to work Busy, for nothing. At the start of your turn, if you have no more Characters in Unemployment than your opponent, gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Open paws, and a tray held out at the height of a kitten. Marmalade's ovens are two streets away and the square smells of them on a cold morning, which the mason did not plan and would not change.
cards.burden: Burden: your opponent's rehires cost 1 less Supply.

cards.name: Statue of Curiosity
cards.text: On gain: draw 2 cards, then discard 1 card. At the start of your turn, look at the top card of your deck and you may send it to your Town Dump.
cards.flavor: Its stone eyes are set on the hill road out of the borough, which is where Comet was looking the two times the board turned her down and the third time it did not.
cards.burden: Burden: at the end of your turn, if you hold more than 6 cards, discard 1.

cards.name: Statue of Courage
cards.text: On gain: your next raise in a Capital City auction costs 1 less Supply to pay. Whenever a bid of yours is tied, toss for it: heads, gain 2 Supply; tails, one of your Characters turns one step toward upright.
cards.flavor: Roger will not call it in the air and never has, but he walks past this one on the way to the fair and everybody in the borough has seen him do it.
cards.burden: Burden: your opponent's first bid each turn is worth 1 more.

cards.name: Statue of Patience
cards.text: Your Masters enter play with one fewer orientation delay (they enter Busy instead of at 180°). At the end of your turn, take a Building token.
cards.flavor: Moss on its shoulders and a chip out of one ear that Barrow has offered four times to mend. It has been there longer than the borough has, and the borough is not finished being built.
cards.burden: Burden: your Apprentices enter Busy instead of upright.

cards.name: Statue of Generosity
cards.text: On gain: give your opponent 1 Supply and draw 2 cards. Whenever Supply is taken from you, gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Arms open and nothing in them. Copper's cellar list is carved on the plinth in letters small enough that you have to kneel, which he says was not his idea and has never asked anyone to take off.
cards.burden: Burden: whenever you gain a Statue, including this one, your opponent gains 2 Supply.

cards.name: Statue of Ingenuity
cards.text: On gain: take 2 Building tokens. Once per turn, an Event you play requires one fewer Character.
cards.flavor: Clever paws, and a mechanism in the stone that has not turned since anybody can remember. Berry looked at it once, said it was never meant to, and went back to the bench.
cards.burden: Burden: your Events cost 1 more Supply.

cards.name: Statue of Community
cards.text: On gain: two of your Characters work together — while both are in your town, each of their shifts pays 1 more Supply. If you control Characters of at least three species, the first shift you complete each turn produces 1 extra Supply.
cards.flavor: Nine figures on one plinth, which is more than the commission asked for and exactly the number of Oatmeal's family. The mason was at the open mic the week before and would not be talked out of it.
cards.burden: Burden: choosing Supply in your Resources phase gives you 1 less.

cards.name: Statue of Harmony
cards.text: Whenever a purchase you are part of resolves with a tied bid, ready one of your Characters at the start of your next turn and gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: A figure with its head tilted, listening. The regatta's called starts are given from its steps, and no cup has ever been argued about twice.
cards.burden: Burden: every pledge you make in an auction must be one step more expensive than the ladder asks.

cards.name: Statue of Joy
cards.text: On gain: ready up to two of your Apprentices. At the end of your turn, take an Entertainment token.
cards.flavor: Carved mid-laugh, which is harder than it sounds and took two winters. It stands where the bandstand's lanterns end, and on open mic nights somebody always puts a hat on it.
cards.burden: Burden: at the start of your turn, give 1 Supply to your opponent.

cards.name: Second Founding
cards.text: Gain 4 Supply, draw 2 cards, ready one of your Characters, and take a Building token.
cards.flavor: The borough has been founded twice: once on the hill, and once the spring Barrow came out from the Capital City and said, in front of everybody, that it was not finished.

cards.name: Founder's Grant
cards.text: Gain 5 Supply and take a Building token.
cards.flavor: Voted at the Counting House, paid in one lump, and spent by most towns inside a fortnight. The chit is the part that lasts.

cards.name: Apprentice Fair
cards.text: Recruit a Character costing 1 or less from your hand for free; it enters upright.
cards.flavor: Held on the green the first fine Saturday in March. Half the borough's trades were settled in an afternoon, and Berry has never once come away without somebody.

cards.name: Guild Intake
cards.text: Recruit a Character costing 2 or less from your hand for free; it enters Busy.
cards.flavor: The engine course runs twice a year and the intake list goes up on the Guild Hall door the week before. Comet took it twice and would take it again.

cards.name: The Spare Room
cards.text: Draw 2 cards, then look at the top two cards of your deck and send any of them to your Town Dump.
cards.flavor: Above the Lending Library, and whoever has it has it until they do not need it. Three of the names on the ward book got their start in it.

cards.name: Second Chances
cards.text: Rehire up to two Characters, each for 2 less Supply.
cards.flavor: Biff's whole method, written down as a line in the budget: stop the trouble, walk them home, and a week later have found them something to do.

cards.name: Old Friends' Reunion
cards.text: Rehire a Character from your Unemployment for free; it enters upright. Then gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: The Hiring Hall's back room, once a year, and nobody has ever called it a reunion to its face. Half its second chances were somebody else's first.

cards.name: Harvest Fair
cards.text: Gain 4 Supply and take a Food token. Your opponent gains 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Quill's press goes all week and the barn holds thirty animals and a queue. Nobody has ever been turned away from it, which is why the neighbouring borough always comes off better than it should.

cards.name: The Watermill
cards.text: Gain 2 Supply, and the next shift you complete produces 2 extra Supply.
cards.flavor: Morty dresses the stone twice a year and will tell you, at length, that the mill is the wheel and not the building. He is right, and it does not help.

cards.name: Ledger Audit
cards.text: Draw 2 cards and look at your opponent's hand.
cards.flavor: Barnaby arrives at four, works through to the morning, and leaves the books squared and a note in the margin about something nobody mentioned. Nobody knows where they are from and the town has decided not to pry.

cards.name: The Town Archives
cards.text: Return an Event from your Town Dump to your hand, then draw 1 card. Goes Out of Play.
cards.flavor: Quinn has four years of it open at once and can put a paw on the one minute you need. He is a mouse and the children are settled that he is a mage, and the archive does nothing to help.

cards.name: The Lucky Horseshoe
cards.text: Toss for it: heads, the next raise against an auction you are winning is cancelled; tails, gain 3 Supply.
cards.flavor: Nailed over the Auction House door the wrong way up, which half the borough says lets the luck out and the other half says pours it on whoever is standing underneath.

cards.name: The Salvage Yard
cards.text: You may discard a card to send an opponent's Character with cost 2 or less to Unemployment. (Cannot target a Character that has not yet been upright on its owner's turn.)
cards.flavor: Patch's counter is a plank across two barrels and the verdict comes over it in about four seconds. What he will not take, Pockets will, and does not say whose it was.

cards.name: The Courier Network
cards.text: Look at the top five cards of your deck and put them back in any order.
cards.flavor: Pebble's tin, Hoot's list and whoever is going that way anyway. It has never been written down and has never once lost anything.

cards.name: The Night Market
cards.text: Gain 2 Supply, then look at the top two cards of your deck and send any of them to your Town Dump.
cards.flavor: It sets up after the gate is shut and packs before the gate is open, and Hazel brought one of its vendors to a daylight committee meeting still in a rumpled night coat.

cards.name: Telescope Hire
cards.text: Look at the top three cards of the Market Deck, then draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Sota reseats the great brass one before he will let anybody near it, and the hire book is kept in Juniper's hand at the top of the observatory steps.

cards.name: The Double Shift Horn
cards.text: Two of your Characters work together: while both are in your town, each of their shifts pays 1 more Supply. Then the next shift you complete produces 1 extra Supply.
cards.flavor: One horn, two animals, and the yard's oldest arrangement: whoever answers it second is working with whoever answered it first, and that is the whole of the rota.

cards.name: The Ironwood Palisade
cards.text: Prevent up to 5 Supply you would lose to opponent effects, and your Characters cannot be sent to Unemployment until your next turn.
cards.flavor: Twice-mended, ivy to the top, and charmingly unimpressive until you try to get over it. Quill leans on the inside of it and is asleep, and nothing has got past yet.

cards.name: The Town Bell
cards.text: Ready one of your Apprentices.
cards.flavor: Rung at six and at six, and once in between for something the borough will talk about for a year. Every apprentice in the wards can tell the difference in their sleep.

cards.name: The Penny Jar
cards.text: Gain 1 Supply and draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Peanut keeps one on the café counter and will not say what it is for. It has been emptied three times, always for somebody else, always the week they needed it.

cards.name: The Chit Tin
cards.text: Take 2 Building tokens and draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Barrow's, kept on the yard wall, and every chit in it is a lot he has measured and priced and not bid on. He says the tin is the useful part.

cards.name: The Surveyor's Table
cards.text: Draw 1 card. Then spend 2 Building tokens: your next Building costs 3 less Supply.
cards.flavor: Adam lays the level across it and the whole county gate road comes off the same sheet. A town that has built before does not pay what a town that has not pays.

cards.name: The Ovens' Account
cards.text: Gain 2 Supply. Then spend 2 Food tokens: ready one of your Food Characters and gain 2 more Supply.
cards.flavor: The borough's ovens are banked overnight and shared out by morning, and the account of who banked what is kept in chalk on the oven door. Food pays for Food; it always has.

cards.name: Warren Muster
cards.text: Take a Rabbit token. Then spend 3 Rabbit tokens: recruit a Character costing 2 or less from your hand for free; it enters upright.
cards.flavor: A conversation outside the Lending Library becomes nine rabbits and a work party, and nobody can say afterwards who called it. Your Rabbits are worth something to each other, which is the only thing one Rabbit is not.

cards.name: Roger's Ha'penny
cards.text: Toss for it: heads, gain 4 Supply; tails, draw 2 cards.
cards.flavor: He has never called it himself, not once, on the grounds that calling it would be taking a side. Somebody else calls it and everybody abides by it, and that is the borough's method for a thing that will not come down on its own.

cards.name: The Long Table
cards.text: Feed two Characters costing 2 or less in your Unemployment; each comes back to work Busy, for nothing.
cards.flavor: Marmalade sets it down the middle of the room on a Sunday and the tray goes round the kittens first. Nobody is hired at it and nobody is paid; they are simply fed, and on Monday they turn up.

cards.name: The Understudy's Shelf
cards.text: Take a Lore token, then look at the top three cards of your deck and send any of them to your Town Dump.
cards.flavor: Andrew keeps it by the late desk: the four books somebody will want at two in the morning, and nothing else, because everything else is upstairs.

cards.name: Bin Round
cards.text: Take an Event out of your opponent's Town Dump into your hand, then draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Pockets at the gate at dusk with a barrow under a sheet, dealing with a carter who is not getting down. Nothing he does is quite a crime; several things are the shape of one, seen from a distance, in poor light.

cards.name: The Mended Mangle
cards.text: Pull one of your Buildings down and put a Building from the City Dump up in its place.
cards.flavor: He sells you back your own mangle, mended, and you thank him for it. The old one goes on the pile and somebody else's comes off it, and the yard is exactly as full as it was.

cards.name: The Late Ferry
cards.text: Take an Otter token for each of your Characters who stood up this turn, then gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Four crossings an hour, every morning, and one more after the gate is shut for whoever is still on the wrong bank. The tin fills on a busy night and does not on a quiet one, which is the whole of the ferry's accounts.

cards.name: A Hard Winter
cards.text: On reveal: every shift in progress in both towns ends at once and produces nothing. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: The year the bridge went, and the cellar under the weights office was not opened. Copper will tell you the list is longer now. He will not tell you what is on the bottom shelf.

cards.name: Sage
cards.title: Night Assistant
cards.text: Recruit: look at the top two cards of your deck and put any of them on the bottom.
cards.flavor: Sage is on the ladder at two in the morning with a serial folded into the watch book, reading ahead in both. Sota grinds the lens and does not ask; Sage tells them anyway.

cards.name: Sage
cards.title: Astronomer
cards.text: Upgrades Sage. When Sage becomes upright, look at the top two cards of the Market Deck, then look at the top two cards of your deck and put any of them on the bottom.
cards.flavor: The sky comes round on a schedule and so does the Capital City, and Sage has never understood why anybody keeps only one of the two lists.

cards.name: Sage
cards.title: Royal Astronomer
cards.text: Upgrades Sage. At the start of your turn, look at the top three cards of the Market Deck and put them back in any order, then look at the top two cards of your deck and put any of them on the bottom.
cards.flavor: The form has been on their desk three times and gone back in the drawer three times. Sage knows the pad, the manifests and the launch window to the minute, and has never put a name on the line. Somebody has to be down here looking, they say, or what is the point of anyone going.

cards.name: Sage’s Star Party
cards.text: Requires Sage and a Science Character. Draw 2 cards, then look at the top two cards of the Market Deck and put them back in any order.
cards.flavor: Bring a blanket. Bring a flask. Do not, under any circumstances, bring a lantern. Sage will read you the bit from the serial where the red world answers, and mean every word of it.

cards.name: Eric
cards.title: Smallholder
cards.text: When Eric is recruited, your next recruit costs 1 less Supply.
cards.flavor: Four rows, a shed and a ledger the lawyers would recognise. He can tell you what the animal in the next field costs to keep, and has, to the animal in the next field.

cards.name: Eric
cards.title: Fair Steward
cards.text: Upgrades Eric. When Eric completes a shift, your next recruit costs 1 less Supply.
cards.flavor: Nine summers on the circuit teach you that everything in the ring has a price on it, including the animals holding the halters. His mother judges the fleeces. His father argues with the almanac.

cards.name: Eric
cards.title: Row Farmer
cards.text: Upgrades Eric. Recruit: you may recruit a Character costing 1 or less from your hand for free; it enters Busy, and if one does, your next recruit costs 1 less Supply.
cards.flavor: He says the figure out loud, in front of them, and it is always better than the one they had got up the nerve to ask for. Nobody has yet worked out how to be insulted by it.

cards.name: Eric
cards.title: Row Boss
cards.text: Upgrades Eric. While Eric is upright, every Character you recruit costs 1 less Supply.
cards.flavor: The whole planting schedule from memory and a stub of chalk, and beside it, in the same hand, what every animal on it is worth for the season.

cards.name: Eric
cards.title: Best Farmer There Ever Was
cards.text: Upgrades Eric. While Eric is upright, every Character you recruit costs 2 less Supply.
cards.flavor: This is the thing the schools and the summers and the seed catalogues were for, and the lawyers are in the ring beside him holding the other end of the rosette, being a nuisance to beat.

cards.name: Benjamin
cards.title: Wick Trimmer
cards.text: Recruit: choose another Character you control; it becomes upright at the start of your next turn.
cards.flavor: He trims every wick on the night round himself and will not be talked out of it. A lamp that gutters on the river path, he says, is a lamp that has told somebody something untrue about where the edge is.

cards.name: Benjamin
cards.title: Lantern Maker
cards.text: Upgrades Benjamin. Busy: return an Event from your Town Dump to the bottom of your deck.
cards.flavor: The blue at the bottom of the flame is the part he is actually looking at, and has been since he was small enough to be carried away from it.

cards.name: Benjamin
cards.title: Town Historian
cards.text: Upgrades Benjamin. Busy: move a shift from one of your Characters to another, then return an Event from your Town Dump to the bottom of your deck.
cards.flavor: Hold the lamp to the beam and he will give you the year, the animal who rebuilt it, the timber it came out of, and a short unkind remark about the joint.

cards.name: Benjamin
cards.title: Master Lantern Maker
cards.text: Upgrades Benjamin. Busy: move a shift from one of your Characters to another, then you may take a card costing 3 or less back out of your Town Dump into your hand.
cards.flavor: Benjamin makes the lanterns and Mandee carries them, and between the two of them the night shift has never stumbled. He fills them at his own bench and nowhere else; that rule is his, not the ward's.

cards.name: Benjamin
cards.title: Keeper of the Light
cards.text: Upgrades Benjamin. At the start of your turn, you may take any card back out of your Town Dump into your hand.
cards.flavor: A fire record is really a record of what a place decided to rebuild, which is why the borough ended up asking a lantern maker about its own history. Light shows us who we truly are. He has been saying it for thirty years and it has been true every time.

cards.name: Jessica
cards.title: Song and Game Leader
cards.text: Recruit: one of your other Characters turns one step toward upright.
cards.flavor: The constellations as a round, with actions. They can all name them. Not one of them can spell any of them. Right, everybody up.

cards.name: Jessica
cards.title: Infant Teacher
cards.text: When Jessica is recruited, your next recruit that upgrades a Character you control costs 1 less Supply.
cards.flavor: She gets them singing the thing before they know it is the thing. By the time a kitten notices they are doing arithmetic they have been doing it for a fortnight and are furious about it.

cards.name: Jessica
cards.title: Night School Teacher
cards.text: Upgrades Jessica. Recruit: one of your other Characters turns one step toward upright, and your next recruit that upgrades a Character you control costs 1 less Supply.
cards.flavor: Lessons begin at ten. Nobody is sure ten what. The animals in that room are not kittens — they are already doing a job and have worked out they would like a better one.

cards.name: Jessica
cards.title: Headmistress
cards.text: Upgrades Jessica. At the start of your turn, your next recruit that upgrades a Character you control costs 2 less Supply.
cards.flavor: She finds the next rung and talks them onto it before they have finished explaining why they could not possibly. Half the Hiring Hall's promotions these ten years started in her room, at ten at night, with a song.

cards.name: Jessica’s Night Class
cards.text: Requires Jessica. Limited 2: at the start of your turn, one of your Characters turns one step toward upright.
cards.flavor: Tonight: fractions, the constellations, and why you should have gone to bed. There is no homework. There has never been any homework.

cards.name: Jake
cards.title: Warren Runner
cards.text: Hired from the Capital City; enters Busy. After two of your turns Jake takes to the road and goes to the bottom of the Market Deck, where he may be hired again. When Jake completes a shift, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: He says what he will do it for, does about three animals' worth of it, and takes the money in his paw rather than on the book. Then one morning the borough looks round and there is no Jake, and no address, and a very tidy row.

cards.name: Faustus
cards.title: Bolt Boy
cards.text: When you announce a purchase with Faustus, gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Nine years old, carrying bolts twice his length, and already telling grown animals what the green does to them in that light. He was right about the green.

cards.name: Faustus
cards.title: Pressure-Suit Tailor
cards.text: Upgrades Faustus. When Faustus is recruited, your challenges cost 1 less Supply until your next turn.
cards.flavor: Fourteen pockets and a tail hole, out of the awful sealed-tin cloth the Science hall sends over. The tail hole was the hard part and he will tell you so, at length, unasked.

cards.name: Faustus
cards.title: Costumier
cards.text: Upgrades Faustus. While Faustus is upright, your challenge bids win ties.
cards.flavor: You do not bring him a drawing. You describe it, badly, waving, and he watches your paws rather than your face and has the bolt down before you finish.

cards.name: Faustus
cards.title: Sailmaker
cards.text: Upgrades Faustus. Busy, once per game: Faustus readies himself.
cards.flavor: A sail is a coat for a boat, darling, and it is cut the same way and priced rather better. He has walked out of a fitting because the light was wrong, and come back at four in the afternoon when it was not.

cards.name: Faustus
cards.title: Threadmaster
cards.text: Hired from the Capital City; enters Busy. While Faustus is displayed in the Capital City, every pledge in an auction must be one step more expensive than usual. While Faustus is upright in your town, that rule falls on your opponent alone.
cards.flavor: He is standing at the Auction House door in something he made this morning, and the whole room has quietly gone up a rung. Buy him and the door is still narrow; it is simply narrow on the other side of you.

cards.name: Thistle
cards.title: Almanac Keeper
cards.text: Busy: your town braces: the next shared shock passes it over.
cards.flavor: It says frost on Tuesday. It has said frost on Tuesday for eleven years, and one day it will be right, and Thistle will not say anything about it then either.

cards.name: Thistle
cards.title: Field Hand
cards.text: Upgrades Thistle. At the start of your turn, your next shift pays 1 more Supply.
cards.flavor: Up before the lanterns, home after the moon. He has never once looked back down the row, and the row keeps up anyway.

cards.name: Thistle
cards.title: Grange Warden
cards.text: Upgrades Thistle. Whenever one of your Characters completes a shift, gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: The grange sends him out with the ones who are sure they are no good at it. It works about nine times in ten, and the tenth is usually a fox.

cards.name: Thistle
cards.title: Field Surveyor
cards.text: Upgrades Thistle. While Thistle is upright, every shift your town finishes pays 1 more Supply.
cards.flavor: He measures the fields with the same long strides that once worked them, and the borough has stopped checking the figures.

cards.name: Thistle
cards.title: Grange Elder
cards.text: Upgrades Thistle. While Thistle is upright, every shift your town finishes pays 2 more Supply.
cards.flavor: Thirty years of exactly the right pace, and a whole grange that works at it without having been told to. Two evenings a month he is at the back of a room with his eyes shut, and gone before the applause, and nobody says a word.

cards.name: Thistle's Grange Supper
cards.text: Requires Thistle and an Agriculture Character. Gain 4 Supply, then you may rehire a Character from your Unemployment for 2 less Supply.
cards.flavor: There is always a chair at the long table for somebody who has been away. Thistle sets it, sits at the far end, and says nothing for two hours, and everybody knows whose supper it is.

cards.name: Tuppence
cards.title: Curio Dealer
cards.text: Hired from the Capital City; enters Busy. At the start of your turn, Buildings cost you 1 less. When Tuppence completes a shift, put 2 Supply by on Tuppence.
cards.flavor: A brass object with a hinge, a crate of ribbed glass the Observatory turned out to want very badly, and a coil of something Moss bought the whole of. Half of what is bolted into this town came off that cart before anybody could say what it was for.

cards.name: Velvet
cards.title: Counter Clerk
cards.text: When Velvet is recruited, Buildings cost you 1 less until your next turn.
cards.flavor: Seventeen years old, out from the Capital City with one good coat, and genuinely thrilled to be handed a counter and a queue.

cards.name: Velvet
cards.title: Notary
cards.text: Upgrades Velvet. Busy, once per game: Velvet readies himself.
cards.flavor: He reads the small print aloud, slowly, all of it, and watches who fidgets. Moss's warning from the Capital City came across this counter and was read at exactly the same pace as everything else.

cards.name: Velvet
cards.title: Neighborhood Registrar
cards.text: Upgrades Velvet. At the start of your turn, Buildings cost you 1 less.
cards.flavor: He is the animal who noticed the far hedgerow turning up in three unrelated files in one spring, and said so, before anybody else had finished reading one of them.

cards.name: Velvet
cards.title: Surveyor of Works
cards.text: Upgrades Velvet. Busy: take down one of your Buildings and raise a Building from the City Dump in its place.
cards.flavor: Nothing goes up in this town and nothing comes down without a form he has read aloud to somebody. Today it is coming down, and he has brought the form outdoors to say so.

cards.name: Velvet
cards.title: Clerk of the Works
cards.text: Upgrades Velvet. At the start of your turn, Buildings cost you 1 less, and 1 less again for every Building you have raised, up to 3 more.
cards.flavor: The consents shelf entire, in one cat, who would not swap it for the Capital City and has been asked twice. The small talk in the queue, he told a public meeting, is the best part of his week. The borough thought about that for a while and decided to believe him.

cards.name: Velvet's Petition
cards.text: Requires Velvet. Draw 1 card. Your next recruit costs 2 less Supply.
cards.flavor: Four hundred signatures, one of them a paw print, and the new hire starts on Monday. Velvet counted all four hundred, twice, and enjoyed it both times.

cards.name: Mandee
cards.title: Night Courier
cards.text: Mandee always arrives upright. When you announce a purchase, look at the top card of the Market Deck.
cards.flavor: At the sorting bench before Hibiscus and gone before Juniper, with Benjamin's lantern on the strap and nothing in the address line at the Hiring Hall.

cards.name: Mandee
cards.title: Weather Watcher
cards.text: Upgrades Mandee. Mandee always arrives upright. Recruit: one of your other Characters turns one step toward upright.
cards.flavor: Red sky at night, Foxes' delight. Red sky in the morning, somebody is bidding. She takes the dome watch at the hour everyone else is turning over, and she takes it standing.

cards.name: Mandee
cards.title: Moonlight Trader
cards.text: Upgrades Mandee. Mandee always arrives upright. While Mandee is upright, your first bid each turn counts as 1 higher.
cards.flavor: She deals after dark, when the prices are honest and the buyers are not, and she is never the animal in the room who has just woken up.

cards.name: Mandee
cards.title: Keeper of Tales
cards.text: Upgrades Mandee. Mandee always arrives upright. Your Master Characters enter Busy rather than two turns from upright.
cards.flavor: The far bank, the long road, the thing at the county line in a bad winter — told at exactly the pace of a walk, and not one of them ever checked. Scott files the whole shelf with the invention and has said once, not as a joke, that he is not sure that is the right shelf.

cards.name: Mandee's Forecast
cards.text: Requires Mandee. Look at the top three cards of the Market Deck, then gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Fine, then wet, then a Statue in the afternoon. She said it on the step at four in the morning and was gone before anybody thought to ask how she knew the third part.

cards.name: Willow
cards.title: Ferry Trader
cards.text: When Willow is recruited, another Character you control is upright at the start of your next turn.
cards.flavor: Nineteen, one bad ferry, and terms the previous owner described for years afterwards as generous of him.

cards.name: Willow
cards.title: Toll Keeper
cards.text: Upgrades Willow. When Willow completes a shift, your opponent puts a card from their hand on top of their deck.
cards.flavor: She uses your name twice a sentence and by the second one you have quietly put away whatever you came in holding.

cards.name: Willow
cards.title: Tide Reckoner
cards.text: Upgrades Willow. Busy: move a shift from one of your Characters to another.
cards.flavor: The tide tables are right to the minute. The harbour runs to Willow's minute, not the tide's, and the tide has never complained where she could hear it.

cards.name: Willow
cards.title: Harbourmaster
cards.text: Upgrades Willow. When Willow becomes upright, your opponent chooses: lose 2 Supply, or put a card from their hand on top of their deck.
cards.flavor: She sets both of the worst outcomes available to you on the table, with enormous warmth, and waits. You will take the less bad one, and on the walk home you will feel that you chose it.

options.label: Put a card back on top of your deck

cards.name: Willow
cards.title: Harbour Admiral
cards.text: Upgrades Willow. Whenever you gain a non-Statue Capital City card, gain 2 Supply. At the start of your turn, your opponent chooses: lose 3 Supply, or one of their Characters is put back to work.
cards.flavor: The boat yard, the towpath cottages, the arcade lease, the harbour office and every licence granted out of it. Pebble's family have a standing rule about never meeting her without a third animal present, and will not say which year they made it.

options.label: Put one of your Characters back to work

cards.name: The Late Desk
cards.text: Requires Andrew and a Lore Character. Take any card back out of your Town Dump into your hand, then draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: The children's corner has emptied and the evening readers have gone, and Andrew is still there with a page and a half to do. What cannot be lent out he copies by hand, a page or two a night, so that there is a second one — and twice now the Library has filed his copy as the original and nobody has corrected it.

cards.name: The Harbour Office
cards.text: Requires Willow and a Civics Character. Gain 2 Supply, and your opponent chooses: lose 2 Supply, or put a card from their hand on top of their deck.

options.label: Put a card back on top of your deck

cards.flavor: Willow started at nineteen with one bad ferry on terms its previous owner described for years as generous of him. She has been writing the terms herself ever since, and they are always two things, and one of them is always the one you did not want to be asked.

cards.name: The Cider Social
cards.text: Requires Quill and an Agriculture Character. Gain 2 Supply, then feed a Character costing 2 or less in your Unemployment; it comes back to work Busy.
cards.flavor: September to February, in the barn, and the Hiring Hall sends whoever is quietly out of work. Quill hands them a basket without ever mentioning it. Rosabeth's garden takes the ones who have stopped getting up; the orchard takes everybody, all the time, so that nobody has to admit to anything.

cards.name: Reading Lanterns
cards.text: Requires a Lore Character. Limited 2: at the start of your turn, draw 1 card.
cards.flavor: Inkwell has the little ones one evening a week and tells them about the worlds on the other side of ours; Lynnette reads on Thursdays, on the floor, doing all the voices. The lanterns are Benjamin's, filled at his bench and nowhere else, and they are hung low enough for a mouse to read by.

cards.name: Tool Lending Day
cards.text: Requires Berry and a Crafts Character. Take a card costing 3 or less back out of your Town Dump into your hand, then gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Half the borough's broken things are queued along the bench and the other half are out on loan. Berry does not mend them for you. Berry puts the thing in your paws, sits on the second stool, and asks what you think is wrong with it, and is still asking an hour later when you have fixed it.

cards.name: The Root Cellar
cards.text: Requires an Agriculture Character. Rehire a Character from your Unemployment for 2 less Supply, then gain 1 Supply.
cards.flavor: Everything off Cookie's board is made to be opened in a different season from the one it was made in — hard biscuit, rusk, seed cake, baked on the late heat of the Community Oven after the bread is out. She dates the shelf in pencil and has never once been wrong about how long it would have to last.

cards.name: A Glut of Squash
cards.text: Requires two Agriculture Characters. Gain 4 Supply, then discard 1 card.
cards.flavor: Thistle set the pace down the row and never once looked back, and now there is more squash than the borough can eat and a grange meeting about it on Thursday. Quill has taken forty for the barn. Morty has taken sixty and will not say what for.

cards.name: The Seed Bank's Open Day
cards.text: Take an Agriculture token and draw 1 card. Then spend 2 Agriculture tokens: recruit a Character costing 2 or less from your hand for free; it enters upright.
cards.flavor: Every variety the First Boroughs have ever grown, dried, doubled and labelled, and one afternoon a year when Maribel puts the drawers out on the trestles. You do not pay for a packet. You come back next autumn with two of them, which she writes down, and that is the whole of the arrangement.

cards.name: The Town Clock
cards.text: Look at the top three cards of the Market Deck and put them back in any order, then your Characters advance an extra step at your next Ready.
cards.flavor: Brass gears, exposed on purpose, and a face the whole square sets its morning by. When it stops the borough calls Berry, and Berry answers to the Town Workshop about it afterwards, and the one thing everybody agrees on is that the hour it strikes is the hour it is.

cards.name: The Market Committee
cards.text: Your opponent chooses: you gain 3 Supply, or you look at the top three cards of the Market Deck, put them back in any order, and draw 1 card.

options.label: Let them set the Capital City deck

cards.flavor: Hazel has run the guild hall twice and sits on the committee in the coat they closed the stall in, and the committee has learned to offer two things it can live with rather than one it cannot. The weathervane over the square is a cat. Nobody will say who paid for that.

cards.name: The Fitting
cards.text: Gain 1 Supply, and your challenges cost 2 less Supply until your next turn.
cards.flavor: You describe it badly, waving, and Faustus has the bolt down before you have finished. He will not make a thing for a room he is not going to be in, which is why the Auction House has stopped pretending that a Mayor who walks in wearing one of his has not already cost everybody a rung.

cards.name: The Toll Gate
cards.text: Gain 1 Supply, then your opponent chooses: lose 3 Supply, or one of their Characters is put back to work.

options.label: Put one of your Characters back to work

cards.flavor: The gate is the borough's, the tolls are the harbour office's, and the season Finn had the keeping of it is mentioned to nobody. Pay it or work it off: the board by the bar has said so since before anybody currently arguing about it was born.

cards.name: The Owl Post
cards.text: Take any card back out of your Town Dump into your hand.
cards.flavor: Hibiscus walks the round and Juniper carries what leaves the borough, and the two of them hand over at the sorting bench at five every morning. Nothing on that round has ever been lost. What has been thrown away is a different question, and the answer is that Hibiscus has it, and knew you would want it back.

cards.name: The Physic Garden
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, you may feed a Character costing 2 or less in your Unemployment; it comes back to work Busy.
cards.flavor: The Capital City built it to grow specimens and the borough uses it to grow animals. Rosabeth will not be drawn on the tinctures — the Science hall has twice failed to account for them — but she is perfectly clear about the rest of it: you are not here to be mended, you are here because the beds want doing.

cards.name: The Weighbridge
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: Every loaded cart in or out of the borough crosses Liz's plate and is paid on what she writes. Copper's office certifies the bridge each spring and has never once had to adjust it, which Copper mentions every spring, and Liz has never once looked up.

cards.name: The Counting House
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: Whenever one of your Characters finishes a shift, gain 2 Supply.
cards.flavor: It budgets for Brett a year ahead and has stopped querying Tuppence's prices, and both of those are Orien's doing: he feeds the shift returns and the auction prices into an engine built out of Observatory cast-offs, and the figure comes back within a Supply.

cards.name: The Town Workshop
cards.title: Capital City Building
cards.text: At the start of your turn, gain 1 Supply. Each of your Events needs one fewer Character.
cards.flavor: It keeps the jigs, the loan book and the standing argument about whether Moss's bench jig counts as the Workshop's now that half the borough uses it. Berry answers to this room when the clock stops and has never once been asked to explain anything else.

cards.name: Six Weeks Shut
cards.text: On reveal: both Mayors lose 2 Supply, then each Mayor may rehire one Character from their Unemployment for free; it enters upright. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: The winter the Grain Exchange shut is one of the borough's two reference points for a bad season. Copper did not open the cellar. He lent the salt out on the quiet instead, said there would be worse, and every animal who was put back to work that February was put back by a neighbour.

cards.name: The Bridge Goes
cards.text: On reveal: both Mayors lose 2 Supply, and at each Mayor's next Ready their Characters do not advance. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: The other reference point, and the spring Adam kept the carts moving the long way round rather than let the borough stop. It cost a day on every load and he has never claimed it as anything. The year the bridge went is how animals here date things.

cards.name: The Eclipse
cards.text: On reveal: both Mayors draw 1 card, and at each Mayor's next Ready their Characters do not advance. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: Sage had the time of it to the minute eleven months out and told anybody who would stand still. Nothing in the borough was done between the quarter hour either side of it, and Jessica's whole night class was out on the hill with smoked glass, which is the sort of homework she does set.

cards.name: The Meteor Shower
cards.text: On reveal: both Mayors draw 1 card and gain 1 Supply. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: Taco's cart moves up to the top of the hill for it, which is the only night of the year anybody can say in advance where the cart will be. Sage counts them aloud. Juniper, who settles even calls by going outside and looking up, has never missed one.

cards.name: The Full Moon
cards.text: On reveal: the Mayor with fewer Statues readies a Character and gains 2 Supply. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: The night round needs no lanterns and Benjamin fills them anyway, on the grounds that a rule kept only on the nights it is needed is not a rule. Hoot knocks the waking list an hour early. Everything in the borough that has been waiting for light gets done between midnight and four.

cards.name: The Cutting Comes Down
cards.text: On reveal: every shift in progress in both towns ends at once and produces nothing, and at each Mayor's next Ready their Characters do not advance. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: The long pull to the county gate is a quarter-hour shorter than the road it replaced, which was Adam's idea, and the cutting that made it shorter is the cutting that came down. He was up there with a lamp before the noise had finished and did not ask anybody to come with him.

cards.name: A Plague of Midges
cards.text: On reveal: each Mayor draws 1 card, then discards down to 4 cards in hand. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: Three days off the water and nothing whatever to be done about it. Bella filed a note on the hatch, cited twice since; Rosabeth sold out of the green tincture by the second morning and gave the rest away; and every meeting in the borough that week was held with the door shut and got through in half the time.

cards.name: A Lean Season
cards.text: On reveal: each Mayor sends one Character of their choice to Unemployment. Goes to the City Dump.
cards.flavor: Not a disaster. A season in which there is simply nothing on, and the Hiring Hall's board is bare by Tuesday. Quinn turns back four years, finds the animals who did that exact work in the last one and has not been asked since, and starts handing out slips with names on them.

newStudies.name: Food
newStudies.blurb: Feeding the town: counters, kitchens, carts and the café. Where Commerce counts the money and Agriculture grows the crop, Food is the animal who hands it over and knows everyone's order.

newStudies.name: Entertainment
newStudies.blurb: The town's evenings: stages, bands, open mic nights, the halls people fill when the shift is over. Civics keeps the town working and Entertainment keeps it worth working for.

townCards.note: The market side of the shelf: Buildings, Events, Market cards, Disruptions and the nine Statues that give the cast, species and studies something to play with. These cards belong to no character entry — a Building is not somebody's backstory — which is why they are listed here. Town Buildings have no art yet: `wantedArt` lists what each one should show, so the illustrations can be commissioned in one batch.

tokens.note: The token shelf. A token is a marker a Mayor holds beside their Supply — never drawn, never bid on, never part of a deck — and each kind is declared by one card here: ten species, eight studies, and one for Buildings. The rules are spec/game.json `tokens`; the engine holds the counts in `player.tokens` and gives, spends and reads them with `gainToken`, `spendToken` and the `tokensAtLeast` condition. The counter was built before any card spent one, deliberately, because tokens are the obvious answer to a whole family of cards the collection keeps reaching for — 'your Rabbits are worth something to each other', 'Food pays for Food', 'the town has built before and it shows' — and every one of those cards wants the same counter underneath it. Those three cards now exist and they are the Warren Muster, the Ovens' Account and the Surveyor's Table: one counter, three cards, none of them inventing their own. Each spends what another card gives — the Chit Tin and the two Founders' cards hand out Building chits, the Harvest Fair a Food chit, the Warren Muster its own first Rabbit — and a price a town cannot meet is not paid at all, so a short holding spends nothing and the card's other half still happens.
